We also establish an exact curvature identity showing that RNLP reproduces the sigma term of NECO without additional assumptions. Finally, we prove the relationships between second-order necessary and sufficient conditions for the two problems. We identify when RNLP can be used to rule out local minimizers of NECO or establish strict local optimality for NECO without explicitly evaluating the sigma term.

papers.title: Probing Dark Matter via the Migdal Effect in LUX-ZEPLIN Data
papers.abstract: Sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles deposit little energy in conventional direct-detection experiments and are therefore difficult to probe, but the Migdal effect provides an electronic signal from atomic ionization accompanying the recoil. Using the new results of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a 4.2 tonne-year exposure, we evaluate the sensitivity of the Migdal effect to the spin-independent DM--nucleon scattering cross section. For masses between $350~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $10~\mathrm{GeV}$, the projected 90\% upper limits range from $6.5\times10^{-37}$ to $9.6\times10^{-42}~\mathrm{cm^2}$. These limits are then used to constrain the minimal scalar- and vector-mediator DM models. For the light-mediator DM model, the constraint on the coupling reaches $\alpha\simeq 10^{-12}$, which is stronger than or comparable to the constraints from kaon decays, stellar cooling, and SN1987A.

papers.title: Spontaneous Formation of Lateral Defect-Density Gradient in CVD-Grown MoS2 Monolayers
papers.abstract: Defect engineering in two-dimensional materials is a powerful strategy for tuning electronic, optical, and catalytic properties. While pristine molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) has been thoroughly studied, defective MoS2 remains poorly understood due to the complexity and inconsistency of controlled defect creation. Here, we report a defect-density gradient that forms spontaneously in MoS2 flakes during chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth. Photoluminescence and Raman spectroscopy mapping reveal the lateral arrangement of this gradient across a single flake. Deconvolution of the excitonic photoluminescence emission identifies electron doping as the key factor governing the spatial variation in optical response. This doping likely originates from sulfur vacancies formed during CVD growth, as further supported by the observed Raman mode shifts. We propose that this gradient arises from precursor depletion near the nucleation center during growth, resulting in a gradual variation in defect density. This lateral defect structure provides a convenient platform for systematically characterizing defective MoS2 across a continuous range of defect densities within a single sample. The sulfur-vacancy-driven surface activation identified here can also be important for future catalytic applications.

papers.title: Renormalon-chain contributions to two-point correlators of nonlocal quark currents and light-meson distribution amplitudes
papers.abstract: In the framework of QCD sum rules, we study the endpoint slopes of the leading-twist distribution amplitudes in the large-$\beta_0$ approximation for the pion and the longitudinally polarized $\rho$ meson. To this end, we compute the two-point massless correlator of non-local composite vector quark currents with the gluon lines dressed by chains of one-loop fermion bubbles. This correlator depends on the Bjorken fraction $x$ associated with the composite current and, within the large-$\beta_0$ approximation, provides the dominant contribution in each order of perturbation theory. We derive an inequality for the second Gegenbauer moments of these distribution amplitudes that agrees with predictions from lattice QCD.

papers.title: Flat "Island of Stability" of Superheavy Nuclei
papers.abstract: We present the first systematic microscopic calculations of fission barrier heights for 292 even-even superheavy nuclei using the multidimensionally constrained relativistic mean field model with triaxial and octupole deformations treated simultaneously. The calculated barrier heights remain around 5 MeV in the vicinity of the predicted doubly magic nucleus ${}^{304}120$. This flat landscape contrasts with the conventional picture of mutually enhanced magicity and indicates that the proton shell closure at $Z=120$ and the neutron shell closure at $N=184$ do not reinforce but suppress each other. We introduce an $\alpha$-linked energy difference $\Delta_{\rm pn}$ to identify the mutually suppressed magicity caused by distinct proton and neutron density distributions. These results challenge the expected shell landscape of superheavy nuclei and may have a crucial impact on estimating survival probabilities in the synthesis of superheavy nuclei.

papers.title: Disentangling Spin and Orbital Contributions in the Search for Altermagnetic Terahertz Conversion in RuO2
papers.abstract: Rutile RuO2 has emerged as a prominent candidate altermagnet, yet the microscopic origin of its reported charge-angular-momentum conversion remains unsettled. Recent theoretical and experimental advances have highlighted a potentially dominant role of orbital transport, raising a fundamental ambiguity between spin- and orbital-mediated conversion in RuO2. Here, we report the first experimental disentanglement of the spin- and orbital-to-charge conversion channels in RuO2 heterostructures using terahertz emission spectroscopy. We identify Fe as a predominantly spin-current injector, whereas Ni and permalloy predominantly inject orbital currents, revealing a substantial orbital contribution to ultrafast terahertz emission. Under controlled spin-current injection, we find no evidence for inverse altermagnetic spin-splitting effect. Instead, the observed anisotropy is consistent with an anisotropic inverse spin Hall response that is strongly conditioned by the near-interface environment. Under orbital-current injection, the anisotropy is markedly weaker, indicating that orbital-to-charge conversion is largely isotropic in RuO2. Our results establish orbital transport and interface-conditioned spin Hall conversion as key to terahertz emission from RuO2, underscoring the need to disentangle spin, orbital, and interfacial contributions before assigning anisotropy to altermagnetism.

papers.title: $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge and exact solution of the $\pm J$ Edwards-Anderson model in a transverse field
papers.abstract: Using the Majorana representation of spin-1/2 operators, we study the $\pm J$ Edwards--Anderson model in a transverse field at $T=0$. We show that, in this representation, the quantity describing the coupling between neighboring spins commutes with the Hamiltonian and, unlike in the Kitaev model, is not subject to any Gauss law. The resulting $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge freedom allows the disorder in the signs of the exchange integrals to be eliminated by an exact gauge transformation, so that the spectrum of the system coincides with that of the model with uniform couplings. The resulting theory is quadratic in the Majorana fields. Computing the local Green's functions, we find that the Edwards--Anderson order parameter vanishes for $\Delta>J\sqrt{Z}$ and equals $1/4$ for $\Delta<J\sqrt{Z}$, which signals a second-order transition from a paramagnetic phase to a spin-glass ground state that is degenerate over spin configurations and replica symmetric at $T=0$.

papers.title: Production of hidden-charm molecular candidates with hidden strangeness in $B_s^0$ decays
papers.abstract: We study the production of spin-one $D_{s0}^*(2317)\bar D_s^*$, $D_{s1}(2460)\bar D_s^*$, and $D_{s1}(2536)\bar D_s^*$ molecular candidates in $B_s^0$ decays with an accompanying $\eta$, providing a complementary probe of their structure and production mechanisms. The meson-loop rescattering amplitudes are constructed from factorized weak sources and heavy-hadron chiral interactions. Constituent couplings are estimated using threshold-dependent compositeness relations, and the associated input uncertainties are propagated to the predicted rates. Opposite-$C$-parity partner hypotheses are included with inherited benchmark parameters. We calculate the branching fractions for two relative signs. Over the cutoff range $2\leq\alpha\leq5$, the larger central branching fractions reach several $10^{-6}$ to several $10^{-5}$, suggesting potential accessibility in future experimental measurements.

papers.title: Group Invariance of Statistical Models and Associated Statistical Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.

papers.title: SEDust: A DUSTY-Based SED-Fitting Pipeline for Dust and Mass-Loss from AGB and LPV Stars
papers.abstract: We present SEDust, an automated pipeline for spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting and the estimation of stellar mass-loss and dust-production rates. We apply this pipeline to quantify the mass-loss and dust injection rates in the dwarf galaxy NGC~6822, focusing on long-period variables (LPVs) and pulsating asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars as major contributors to dust feedback into the interstellar medium. The total stellar mass-loss rate is found to be $(3.70 \pm 1.16) \times 10^{-3}\ M_{\odot} \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Two alternative methods (an LPV-based estimate and DESK) give totals that differ from this value by factors of $\sim$2.3 (lower) and $\sim$2.4 (higher), respectively, which we adopt as an estimate of the method-dependent systematic uncertainty. A positive correlation between stellar luminosity, intrinsic reddening caused by circumstellar dust self-extinction, and mass-loss rate is observed. The specific mass-return rate from AGB stars is $(7.40 \pm 2.30) \times 10^{-11}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, indicating that mass return from AGB stars alone is insufficient to sustain the current star formation rate of NGC~6822. This result implies the need for external gas accretion or additional mass-return mechanisms.

papers.title: Strong phonon-coupled trion emission in Janus homobilayer
papers.abstract: Janus transition metal dichalcogenides with broken mirror symmetry provide a novel platform for exploring many-body effects mediated by spin-valley-phonon interactions. Strong electron-phonon coupling demands a precise match between a strong effective dipole moment and nanometer-scale charge confinement. Here, we report thermally robust and enhanced trion emission in a symmetric bilayer WSeS with an S/S stacking configuration. The inward-pointing antiparallel built-in electric fields induce a strong electron confinement effect at the interface, driving dominant trion emission at cryogenic temperatures. Furthermore, a massive electron-phonon coupling strength (3.9) resonant with the optical phonon A_1^2 energy (51 meV) contributes to the thermal stability of this trion emission at elevated temperatures. By tailoring the interfacial architecture in Janus WSeS homobilayers, this study overcomes the thermal decoherence limits inherent to traditional semiconductor systems, offering novel insights into room-temperature many-body interactions.

papers.title: Cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension
papers.abstract: We define cuspidal sections for varieties of arbitrary dimension over fields of characteristic zero, extending the definition for curves by Grothendieck. Our notion of cuspidal sections is defined relative to a normal crossings compactification. We prove that the closure of the resulting set is independent of the choice of a compactification. For varieties iteratively constructed from fibrations, we compare our definition to an inductive notion of cuspidal sections, and discuss connections to the section conjecture of Grothendieck.

papers.title: Slim Polygons, Hyperbolicity, and a new Quasi-Isometric Invariant
papers.abstract: We introduce the slimness function, $\mathrm{Slim}_X(n)$, of a geodesic metric space, which records the maximal slimness of its geodesic polygons as a function of the number of sides. We study the large-scale behaviour of this function and its relation to hyperbolicity, growth function, and quasi-isometries. We first establish that the slimness function is a natural quasi-isometric invariant in the hyperbolic setting. We then obtain quantitative estimates for geodesic polygons in hyperbolic spaces and bounded-valency graphs. In particular, we show that sufficiently slow growth of the slimness function forces tree-like geometry. We also prove a decomposition result for hyperbolic groups admitting a finite graph of hyperbolic groups decomposition. Finally, we investigate the interaction between polygonal slimness and the growth of connected bounded-valency graphs. Combining the resulting estimates with large-scale dimension theory, we obtain criteria implying that an unbounded graph has asymptotic dimension one.

papers.title: Quantitative group testing with a fixed shore: sharp asymptotics and exact formulas
papers.abstract: We study adaptive quantitative group testing with one defective item in each of two disjoint sets. When one set has fixed size, we determine the leading term of the difference between the binary bound and the largest searchable opposite set size. The result extends to fixed unions of complete bipartite graphs and to positive weighted sums of the opposite set sizes. We determine exact eventual formulas when the fixed set has six, seven or eight items. The eight-item formula has a period-three correction. We explain this correction by optimizing the sizes of shared test pieces within fixed decision-tree prefixes. For each fixed finite family of such prefixes ending in star forests, the optimal deficit is eventually a rational polynomial plus a bounded periodic function. The asymptotic proofs are analytic; the exact formulas also use integer constructions and rational exclusion certificates.

papers.title: Characterization of Attenuated V-Line Transform and Direct Reconstruction from Samples
papers.abstract: The V-line transform (V-LT), a generalized Radon transform (RT), is widely used in Compton scattering imaging (CSI). The central mathematical problem of CSI is to reconstruct a function from its V-LT. Unlike V-LT, the attenuated V-line transform (AV-LT) accounts for the medium-induced loss of intensity, and has been demonstrated to improve image quality. The present paper makes two main contributions. (1) We establish the fundamental characterizations for AV-LT including operator properties ($L^2$-boundedness, operator norm etc.), a necessary and sufficient condition for the preservation of compact support, and sharp estimation of Sobolev smoothness. These characterizations remain unexplored, and they reveal essential differences among AV-LT, RT and V-LT. (2) We develop a direct reconstruction method based on AV-LT samples that does not require solving any equation. Our sampling formula gives exact reconstruction for band-limited functions. We also provide approximate reconstruction for functions in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with $s>2$.

papers.title: Claw-free minimal factor-critical and bicritical graphs
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ is called $k$-factor-critical if $G-S$ has a perfect matching for every subset $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|=k$, and is minimal if $G-e$ is not $k$-factor-critical for every edge $e$ of $G$. The cases $k=1$ and $k=2$ correspond to factor-critical and bicritical graphs, respectively. In this paper, we obtain complete structural characterizations of claw-free minimal factor-critical graphs and claw-free minimal bicritical graphs. The former is characterized by ear decompositions. For the latter, we first characterize the $3$-connected case using the theory of line graphs and then extend the characterization to the general case by a suitable $2$-sum operation.

papers.title: Complete uniqueness for two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows
papers.abstract: Alt, Caffarelli and Friedman established the existence of two-dimensional asymmetric incompressible jet flows in [Asymmetric jet flows. Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 35, 29--68, 1982]. In their formulation, the constant fluid speed $\lambda$ on the free boundaries and the downstream asymptotic angle $\theta$ are selected as part of the solution. In this paper, we prove that the asymmetric jet is unique for a prescribed nozzle and mass flux. We first establish the strict vertical monotonicity of the stream function $u$ and introduce the partial hodograph coordinates $\xi=x$ and $\eta=u(x,y)$, which map every fluid domain onto the same fixed strip. Under this framework, each jet is characterized by a height function $y=h(\xi,\eta)$, which determines the vertical position along the streamline $u=\eta$ at horizontal coordinate $\xi$. By analyzing the difference between the height functions of two candidate jets on this strip, we derive an elliptic equation with Dirichlet conditions on the fixed walls and conormal conditions on the free boundaries. Combining these mixed boundary conditions with the asymptotic behaviors, we first establish the uniqueness of the free-boundary fluid speed $\lambda$. For the resulting common speed, a local perturbation of the height function near a nozzle endpoint, together with the maximum principle, proves that the two height functions must coincide. Inverting the partial hodograph transformation then establishes the uniqueness of the physical jet.

papers.title: Coulomb screening of the orbital inverse Faraday effect in finite-size diffusive conductors
papers.abstract: We study the effects of Coulomb screening on the second-order dc response in finite-size diffusive conductors. Starting from the Boltzmann equation supplemented by the self-consistent electrostatic field, we develop a kinetic theory of the inverse Faraday effect for a two-dimensional disk driven by a circularly polarized ac electric field. In this formulation, the first-order charge modulation and the induced electric field are coupled through the Coulomb interaction, and the self-consistent first-order solution determines the nonlinear source for the second-order dc circulating current responsible for the induced magnetic moment. The radial problem is solved numerically using an angular-harmonic expansion and the Chebyshev collocation method. It is shown that in the non-self-consistent approximation the frequency dependence of the second-order dc response has a maximum when the diffusion length associated with the radiation frequency becomes comparable to the sample radius. This behavior is found to be strongly modified by self-consistent screening. We demonstrate that Coulomb screening shifts the maximum of the dc response to a higher drive frequency and suppresses the peak amplitude. This behavior is observed consistently for the area-integrated circulating current and the induced magnetic moment. The obtained results clarify the limitations of the non-self-consistent description of the inverse Faraday effect and show that Coulomb self-consistency is crucial for quantitative predictions of optically induced dc magnetization in finite-size diffusive conductors.

papers.title: Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations
papers.abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of $2$ and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman--Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems. When the affinity dimension is at most an explicit threshold determined by the Lyapunov exponents, the formula holds assuming only that there are no exact overlaps. Above the threshold, it holds under the strong open set condition. These dimension formulae are proved by approximation with finite diagonal subsystems. Assuming projective exponential separation, we also determine the pointwise dimensions of the coordinate projections of the equilibrium state. Below the threshold, the projections are not exact-dimensional: the pointwise dimension of each exists almost everywhere and takes exactly two values, each on a set of positive measure. At or above the threshold, both projections are exact-dimensional with dimension one.

papers.title: Ore-degree conditions for matchings in uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: Let $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})$ be the minimum sum of vertex degrees over all nonedges of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ on $n$ vertices. Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi conjectured that $n>2rs$ and $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ imply the existence of a matching of size $s$ in $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that, for every fixed $r\ge3$ and all sufficiently large $s$, $\sigma_r(\mathcal{H})>r[\binom{n-1}{r-1}-\binom{n-s}{r-1}]$ forces an $s$-matching whenever $n\ge rs+\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$. A complete $r$-graph on $rs-1$ vertices together with $\lfloor(r-1)^{r-1}/r^{r-2}\rfloor$ isolated vertices shows that the vertex bound is sharp for all sufficiently large $s$. By adding new vertices to $\mathcal{H}$, retaining all its edges, and adding every $r$-set containing at least one new vertex as an edge, we also deduce that $n\ge rs+C$ suffices under the same degree condition for every $s\ge1$, where $C$ is a finite constant depending only on $r$. For $r=3$, we provide the explicit sufficient order $n\ge\lceil(7s+11)/2\rceil$ for $s\ge6$, together with bounds for $2\le s\le5$, establishing the conjecture in this uniformity. For $s=2$, we improve the known sufficient order $2r+2$ to $2r+1$ for every $r\ge3$ and show that this order is best possible.

papers.title: Cable Knot Counterexamples to the All-Knot Volume Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be the figure-eight knot and let $V$ be the hyperbolic volume of its exterior. We study the reduced colored Jones polynomial at $q=e^{2\pi i/N}$ for the $(p,w)$-cable of the connected sum of $d\ge 2$ copies of $E$, where $w\ge 2$ and $p,w$ are coprime. The normalized logarithmic growth rate converges to the JSJ volume $dV$ along colors coprime to $2w$, and its upper limit along colors sharing a divisor with $w$ is at most $V$. Thus the $(1,2)$-cable of $E\#E$ violates the full-sequence volume limit for knots. The $(1,3)$-cable of the same companion shows that convergence can fail even along all odd colors. The separation comes from the multiples of $N$ in the exact cabling sum and a uniform first-derivative estimate for the other companion colors.

papers.title: Analogue Schwinger Pair Production in Acoustic Black Holes
Fair Selection of Generalized Nash Equilibria: A Comparability Perspective
papers.abstract: Generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problems model self-interested agents coupled through their costs and shared constraints, and arise throughout control applications that allocate a scarce common resource. Such problems typically admit a continuum of equilibria, so any implementation must \emph{select} one. This selection is not neutral: it decides how the cost of the shared constraint is distributed among the agents, a decision often expected to be fair. The variational GNE (v-GNE), which charges all agents a uniform shadow price, is the conventional choice and is frequently advocated as fair. Through the lens of \emph{comparability} from social choice theory, we show that the GNE set itself requires no inter-agent comparability of costs, whereas the v-GNE implicitly assumes cardinal unit comparability, one of the stronger notions. We then introduce the fair GNE (f-GNE), which selects an equilibrium by explicitly optimizing a fairness metric matched to the comparability at hand, and give constructive routes to compute it for single-constraint and linear-quadratic games. An electric-vehicle charging game serves as a running example throughout this self-contained tutorial.

papers.title: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.

papers.title: Zariski dense hyperbolic 3-manifold groups in $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$
papers.abstract: We show that $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$ contains an infinite family of Zariski-dense subgroups isomorphic to the fundamental group of a fixed closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, which are pairwise noncommensurable up to conjugacy.

papers.title: Resolvent-Diagonal Energy of Isospectral Jacobi Matrices
papers.abstract: We study the minimum squared resolvent diagonal among Jacobi matrices with prescribed eigenvalues. For the zeros of $P_n^{(\alpha,\beta)}$, we construct a canonical realization and bound its asymptotic cost against the optimum. Its rescaled inverse converges to the Green operator of a reflection-symmetric singular Schrödinger operator with Bessel-zero spectrum. A Green-coordinate identity places this construction and all finite realizations in the same density framework. Mass-constrained spectral problems then give computable lower bounds. The bounds meet at $\alpha=1/2$, with optimal energy $2/15$, and have first-order contact with derivative $-13/75$. We classify the constrained extremal profiles and the three endpoint geometries of the canonical density. Two polynomial families with the same limiting edge spectrum have different limiting optimal energies. For Nesterov momentum $(s-1)/(s+1)$, the optimal leading endpoint Hessian-drift gain among nonnegative-link Jacobi realizations is $\sqrt{2}$ times the original gain. An explicit isospectral flow strictly improves the standard one-sided realization for $\alpha>-1/2$, $\alpha\ne1/2$.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of high-index saddle dynamics
papers.abstract: High-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) has been extensively adopted to compute saddle points of arbitrary index, with various applications such as constructing solution landscapes of complex systems. In this work, we prove the asymptotic stability of various HiSD methods, including the idealized, perturbed, and coupled HiSD methods, as well as their momentum-accelerated variants. The analysis is Jacobian-free and thus compensates for the linear stability analysis in the literature. The results not only provide specific characterizations for the convergence rate and the basin of attraction, but also reveal intrinsic correlations among dynamics in the coupled HiSD. Theoretical results are substantiated by numerical experiments.

papers.title: Phosphorus-rich star formation in giant molecular clouds hosting primordial globular clusters
papers.abstract: Recent observational studies have identified phosphorus-rich (P-rich) stars ([P/Fe]>1.0) in both Galactic globular clusters (GCs) including three confirmed cases and the field population. Using analytical models of GC formation, we investigate a scenario in which P-rich stars form from pristine gas in GC-forming giant molecular clouds (GMCs) polluted by oxygen-neon (ONe) novae within and surrounding the GMCs. Within this framework, we model the chemical abundance patterns of P-rich stars using diverse chemical yield sets for ONe novae while varying the dilution factor (Fdil), defined as the ratio of pristine gas mass to total ONe nova ejecta mass. The principal results of our models are as follows: Across a wide range of Fdil, most models display positive correlations between [P/Fe], [N/Fe], [O/Fe], [Al/Fe]$, [Si/Fe], [S/Fe], and [Si/S]. The [Ce/Fe] ratios in P-rich stars can reach values up to 1 if the GMCs are additionally polluted by interacting low-mass asymptotic giant branch stars.P-rich star formation is highly unlikely in environments with a low interaction frequency between GMCs and ONe novae. P-rich stars exhibit anomalously low 14N/15N, 16O/17O, and 16O/18O isotopic ratios, offering a clear observational diagnostic to test this scenario. Assuming that P-rich Galactic field stars originate from GCs, we discuss the origin of their chemical abundance patterns. We suggest that the existence of P-rich stars provides direct evidence that GC-forming GMCs were polluted by pre-existing stellar populations.

papers.title: Dynamical formation of Gaia neutron star binaries in star clusters as a phase-dependent process
papers.abstract: Gaia has discovered dormant compact-object binaries in which the compact object shows no observable interaction with its luminous companion. These systems, hereafter Gaia BHs and Gaia NSs for black hole (BH) and neutron star (NS) companions, provide a new probe of compact-object binary formation. These detached systems are difficult to produce through standard isolated binary evolution alone, and their formation pathways remain unclear. Previous $N$-body studies have shown that Gaia BH-like objects are formed efficiently in star clusters, while Gaia NS-like objects are not. This has been attributed to the BH subsystem dominating the cluster core. We performed direct $N$-body simulations of $10^4 \mathrm{M}_\odot$ star clusters in a Galactic tidal field and investigated how NS-main-sequence (NS-MS) binaries form during the late BH-depleted phase. We found that NS-MS binaries satisfying Gaia-sensitive criteria form only after BH depletion. NSs are present in the core throughout the evolution, but the strong encounters there are monopolized by the BH subsystem until it is depleted. Our results show that the dynamical formation of Gaia-sensitive NS-MS systems is not prevented in star clusters, but delayed relative to Gaia BH-like systems.

papers.title: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos
The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
papers.abstract: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $\mu \to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.

papers.title: Baryon Number Susceptibilities of Hot and Dense Nuclear Matter in Relativistic Mean-Field Models
papers.abstract: We develop a fully analytical framework for calculating baryon number susceptibilities in relativistic mean-field (RMF) models of hot and dense nuclear matter at finite temperature and baryon chemical potential. The formalism is applied to representative nonlinear RMF parameterization sets to investigate the model dependence of baryon number fluctuations over a wide range of temperatures and baryon chemical potentials. All the considered RMF parameterizations reproduce the overall qualitative beam-energy dependence of the cumulant ratios. The observed skewness and kurtosis within the RMF models satisfy the experimental values. Specifically, the FSU-family parameterizations exhibit relatively small deviations from the measured heavy-ion observables i.e. cumulant ratios.

papers.title: Induction instead of Feynman diagrams, L-functionals instead of Hilbert space
The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields, II
papers.abstract: We prove that every number field of odd degree $n\geq 3$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has an integral defining polynomial whose coefficients are $O_n(D^{(n-1)/(2n-1)})$ in size. This strengthens, in odd-degree cases, the recently established bound of $O_n(D^{1/2})$ for all degrees $n$, which was conjectured in 1998 by Ruppert and is now known to be optimal in even degrees. More generally, we prove that this strengthened bound holds for all degree-$n$ fields having a real embedding and no subfield of index two. The proof makes use of the lattice shapes of the ring of integers and its trace dual, the inverse different. Assuming the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions, as recently announced by Cureton and Thorner, we obtain an exponent smaller than $1/2$ for every field with no index-two subfield, of any signature. In the case of primitive fields, we obtain the exponent $(n-1)/(2n)$. In particular, we prove that the optimal exponent for cubic fields is $1/3$.

papers.title: Delaunay classification of positive singular solutions to the critical Lane--Emden system
papers.abstract: We classify positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system \begin{align*} \begin{cases} -\Delta u=v^p & ~~\text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\},\\ -\Delta v=u^q &~~ \text{in }\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}, \end{cases} \end{align*} with a nonremovable singularity at $0$ (i.e., $\lim_{x\to0}u(x)=\lim_{x\to0}v(x)=+\infty$), where $n\ge3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy \[ \frac1{p+1}+\frac1{q+1}=\frac{n-2}{n}. \] Without additional growth or integrability assumptions, we establish radial symmetry about the origin, strict radial decrease, and global two-sided power bounds for both components. Furthermore, every such solution can be written as \[ u(x)=|x|^{-\alpha}U(\log|x|),\qquad v(x)=|x|^{-\beta}V(\log|x|), \] where $\alpha=\frac{n}{q+1}$, $\beta=\frac{n}{p+1}$, and $(U,V)$ is either the positive equilibrium $(A,B)=((\frac{\alpha}{\beta})^{\frac{\alpha}{2}}, (\frac{\alpha}{\beta})^{\frac{\beta}{2}})$ or a positive nonconstant periodic solution of the associated Emden--Fowler system. These periodic solutions form a Delaunay family: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,A)$, there is a unique profile pair, up to translation in $t=\log|x|$, with $\min_{\mathbb{R}}U=\varepsilon$. The Hamiltonian energy provides an alternative parameter, decreasing continuously and strictly from zero to the equilibrium energy as $\varepsilon$ increases from $0$ to $A$. The common least period of the two components tends to infinity as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and to the period of the linearized oscillation at $(A,B)$ as $\varepsilon\uparrow A$. The classification includes the case of a sublinear exponent.

papers.title: Symmetry-Gated Sliding: Decoupling Interlayer Translation from Polarization Reversal in Boron Nitride Ferroelectrics
papers.abstract: Electric-field-driven polarization switching in sliding ferroelectrics depends on how local interlayer motion is accommodated by the surrounding structure. Yet the relationship between sliding, domain-wall (DW) propagation, and collective domain evolution under changing vector fields remains unclear. Here, we show that local symmetry governs the coupling between field-induced forces and interlayer sliding, while DW connectivity determines how local motion contributes to net domain conversion. These effects are examined across three structural scales, from monodomains and isolated DWs to reconstructed moire networks. We investigate bilayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) using molecular dynamics with a machine-learning interatomic potential that incorporates field-dependent electric enthalpy. An initially monodomain bilayer switches through directional wrinkling and interlayer sliding, while the barrier along a constrained flat path remains finite. Pre-existing DWs propagate with velocities governed by their shear and tensile character, and an additional in-plane field tunes wall velocity and width according to its orientation. In reconstructed triangular moire networks, shared junctions and boundary curvature mediate domain evolution and recovery after field removal or reversal. Most strikingly, a rotating in-plane field translates the layers and displaces the moiré nodes by approximately 1 AA yet leaves the AB/BA domain-area ratio without detectable change, because threefold connectivity cancels the contributions of individual walls. We term this response polarization-silent sliding. These results distinguish local sliding, DW translation, and net domain conversion as different responses to electric fields and establish how local structural symmetry and DW connectivity shape their selective control.

papers.title: Constrained Nested-Logit Pricing: An Exact Reformulation and Global Optimization Method
papers.abstract: Sellers must price substitutable products while meeting operational requirements such as price limits and sales targets. Nested logit captures stronger substitution among similar products, but these requirements can undermine the structure used to solve unconstrained pricing problems. We develop an exact reformulation and a global optimization method for a fixed assortment with price bounds and weighted price caps. The key novelty is to concentrate the difficult interactions at the nest level while retaining convex optimization over individual products, without discretizing prices or approximating demand. This structure makes the number of nests, rather than products, govern the exponent in a conditional worst-case complexity bound. The method returns feasible prices together with a bound on how much profit could still be gained, allowing decision makers to assess solution quality even when computation stops early. Extensions cover purchase-probability bounds and price-order rules, with explicit accounts of their computational cost. In synthetic experiments, the method certifies solutions for assortments of up to 500 products with few nests. Projecting unconstrained prices onto the feasible set loses up to 32.60% of profit relative to direct constrained optimization, highlighting the value of jointly optimizing substitution and feasibility.

papers.title: Infinitely many convex polytopes with dihedral angles bounded above by $π/2+δ$
papers.abstract: For every $\delta>0$, we construct infinitely many pairwise combinatorially distinct convex three-dimensional polytopes whose dihedral angles are all less than $\pi/2+\delta$.

papers.title: Perfect Wave Transfer in Nonconformal Tomonaga-Luttinger Liquids
papers.abstract: Perfect wave transfer (PWT) reproduces spatial reflection at a common finite time under a fixed Hamiltonian. We classify this process for open compact bosons and inhomogeneous Tomonaga--Luttinger liquids, distinguishing transfer of oscillator and neutral observables from transfer on the charged field algebra. In the single-charge model, the first two notions coincide. Global transfer additionally requires rephasing of the compact zero mode. For regular reflection-symmetric channels, exact oscillator transfer forces an odd multiple of the optical crossing time and a strictly ordered, parity-compatible spectrum differing from the conformal ladder at only finitely many levels. This spectral condition is also sufficient when the Robin boundary data induced by the physical profile are included. Requiring Neumann conditions after the Liouville transformation instead forces conformality. We construct an explicit, regular one-defect family for every $r>1/2$. Its transfer parameters are precisely the reduced fractions $r=p/q$ with odd numerator and denominator, with shortest transfer time $pL/v_0$. At the delay $3L/v_0$, the $r=3/5$ profile has numerical contrast $K_{\max}/K_{\min}\simeq 12.913$, compared with $81$ for $r=3$. Two independent conservative discretizations show second-order convergence on fixed mode bands. Occupation- and charge-constrained error estimates quantify robustness, while an exact homogeneous-chain calculation explains the $J^{2/3}$ resolved-band scale also observed in the engineered channels. These results provide a spectral design method and finite-device benchmarks for quadratic quantum channels. An interacting microscopic realization remains open.

papers.title: Twisted Verlinde Formula for Finite Cyclic Orbifolds of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite and self-dual vertex operator algebra of CFT type, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic automorphism group of $V$. We establish a twisted Verlinde formula for cyclic groups of arbitrary finite order, expressing fusion coefficients among twisted $V$-modules in terms of the $S$-matrix in the orbifold theory. As an application, we compute fusion rules among twisted modules for the permutation orbifold $\left(V^{\otimes k}\right)^{\langle g\rangle}$ associated with a $k$-cycle $g=(1\,2\,\cdots\,k)$.

papers.title: On optimal convergence rates for parametrized variational problems with applications to nonlocal models
papers.abstract: We develop an abstract variational framework for convergence rates of parametrized problems and their Galerkin approximations, with applications to nonlocal diffusion. The main objective is to quantify modeling and discretization errors in terms of the nonlocal horizon, the mesh size, the Sobolev regularity of the local solution, and the compatibility of boundary data. We establish error estimates in energy and $L^2$ norms and develop an adaptation of the Aubin--Nitsche argument that uses regularity of the limiting local dual problem. This approach yields improved $L^2$ estimates without requiring additional regularity of the nonlocal dual solutions, including for integrable kernels. We apply the framework to two constant-horizon nonlocal Laplacians with exterior boundary data and to heterogeneous localization models with classical Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions. The resulting estimates provide quantitative guarantees of asymptotic compatibility and improve existing error bounds under weaker regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence rates and examine the sharpness of the estimates.

papers.title: Walsh Analysis in the Twenty-First Century: Convergence, Summability, Nonlinear Approximation, Universality, and Digital Applications
papers.abstract: Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables. The concluding problems separate source-listed questions, proposed refinements, and elementary obstructions. Supplementary derivations preserve normalization checks and finite covariance calculations while keeping the main exposition focused on the analytic mechanisms.

papers.title: Critical Resonance and the Radial Branch in Maz'ya's Weighted Hessian--Gradient Inequality
papers.abstract: We study the sharp constant $C(p,\gamma)$ in Maz'ya's planar weighted inequality \[ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|\nabla\psi|^p|x|^{p(\gamma-1)}\, \mathrm{d} x \le C(p,\gamma)\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}|D^2\psi|_{\mathrm{F}}^p|x|^{p\gamma}\, \mathrm{d} x, \] where $|\cdot|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. For every fixed $1\le p<\infty$, with $a=\gamma-1+2/p$, we prove \[ C(p,\gamma)^{-1}=2^{p/2}|a|^p+O_p(|a|^{p+1})\qquad(a\to0). \] The leading term comes from the first angular harmonics after the Emden--Fowler transform. We also determine explicit exterior parameter rays on which the unrestricted constant equals the radial value $(1+a^2)^{-p/2}$. The proof uses an entropy identity and a homogeneous calibration. In the remaining transition region, we obtain symmetry-breaking intervals and a necessary and sufficient condition for nonnegativity of the periodic second variation at the radial state. An explicit example shows that global symmetry breaking can occur even when this second variation is nonnegative.

papers.title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].

papers.title: Supporting Data Center Grid Integration via Co-Optimized Battery Energy Storage Sizing and Capacity Allocation
papers.abstract: Interconnecting large data centers can be delayed by grid requirements on demand flexibility, ramping limits, and ride-through performance. This paper proposes an optimization-based framework to size a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) that accelerates data center grid integration by providing BESS capacity required to meet selected flexibility and grid-support requirements. The model co-optimizes BESS power rating and energy capacity while allocating capability across three services: (i) demand response over a specified duration, (ii) mitigation of high-magnitude, high-frequency load fluctuations through reserved active power with zero net state-of-charge change, and (iii) voltage support via reactive power capability at the point of common coupling. Minute-level operational scheduling enforces state-of-charge feasibility and load ramp constraints, and incorporates a controllable queue of delay-insensitive computing tasks to enhance flexibility. A case study using a real data center load profile demonstrates the proposed method and quantifies the BESS power-energy requirements and operational trade-offs needed to satisfy the multi-service constraints, providing practical guidance for interconnection planning and deployment.

papers.title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
papers.abstract: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.

papers.title: Calibrating your confidence requires thinking of all the ways you could be wrong
papers.abstract: A primary limitation of modern deep learning is the miscalibration of model confidence; traditional architectures fundamentally lack a mechanism to quantify their own uncertainty. Larger models and larger datasets mitigate this issue, but they do not resolve the underlying structural deficiency. Bayesian methods offer a principled uncertainty-aware learning framework through stochastic parameters. Yet, despite the established benefits, the inherent computational overhead often compromises either scalability or quality. This trade-off currently prevents the widespread adoption of Bayesian methods. This Thesis bridges the gap between high-quality and low-complexity by introducing a novel distribution on parameter space: a degenerate Gaussian whose covariance is a projection matrix aligned with the null space of the Fisher information matrix. We demonstrate the scalability of this Bayesian posterior through two numerically efficient algorithms: one for posterior sampling and another for the direct computation of predictive confidence. Empirically, we show State-Of-The-Art confidence calibration and out-of-distribution detection for large models. We provide theoretical grounding for this approach. We study the degeneracies inherent in Amari's information geometry and highlight its most relevant component: the split of parameter's perturbations into two orthogonal subspaces. From this perspective, our posterior naturally emerges as the simplest choice that captures this split, assigning unitary variance to one subspace and zero variance to the other. Moreover, through the tools of differential geometry, we utilize this split to identify and rectify a critical misalignment issue of the non-linearized Laplace Approximation. Finally, with a focus on PAC-Bayes generalization bounds, we pave the way for a deeper understanding of the learning capabilities of overparametrized models.

papers.title: Enforcing Symmetries on Pre-trained ML Models for Physics
papers.abstract: Post-hoc group averaging (or test-time augmentation) is a simple way to impose symmetry on a trained predictor without changing its architecture or retraining it. For finite and compact groups, averaging over a normalized Haar measure on the group gives the Reynolds operator: a canonical projection onto invariant or equivariant predictors with known non-increasing risk guarantees under certain assumptions. This paper provides numerical experiments on physics emulation models that demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in this setting. We then extend this framework to non-compact group symmetries. For non-compact groups, the Haar measure cannot be normalized, so group averaging cannot be defined in the same way. We replace it with three alternatives: the Weyl unitary trick (which requires complexifying the space and extending the predictor), a data-dependent orthogonal projection (which involves a non-trivial optimization on the space of invariant or equivariant functions), and a frame averaging approach (which involves mapping each point to a set of orbit representatives). We illustrate the constructions theoretically and empirically on the unit-rescaling group and the Lorentz group. Our results show that in the non-compact case, the Weyl trick and frame averaging do not provide a consistent improvement over the baseline, except where the test data is out-of-distribution (an orders-of-magnitude improvement in this case) and, for the Weyl trick, in low-data regimes. The orthogonal projection can provide improvements in-distribution and out-of-distribution. We also observe that models trained directly on invariant features matched or beat the projection of an unconstrained one. We conclude that post-hoc symmetrization extends to non-compact groups, but it does not consistently outperform training a symmetric model.

papers.title: Finite-rank Toeplitz commutators on the harmonic Bergman space
papers.abstract: We completely characterize finite-rank commutators of Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk. Apart from affine dependence, finite rank occurs precisely when both symbols are analytic with rational primitives, or both are coanalytic and their complex conjugates have rational primitives. Our approach combines a block-matrix decomposition with Luecking's theorem, which rules out nonzero finite-rank Toeplitz operators with bounded symbols on the Bergman space. In particular, every such finite-rank commutator has square zero.

papers.title: Native point defects in rock-salt and wurtzite MnSe: formation energies across the growth window and spin splitting in the A-type order
papers.abstract: Manganese selenide grows both as rock-salt $\alpha$-MnSe, a type-II antiferromagnet, and as metastable wurtzite w-MnSe, whose magnetic order has not been measured. We compute the neutral Mn and Se vacancies and the two antisites of both polymorphs with density functional theory plus a linear-response Hubbard $U$, between the Se-rich limit bounded by MnSe$_2$ and the Mn-rich limit set by the measured formation enthalpy. In $\alpha$-MnSe the Mn vacancy is lowest over most of the window (0.92 eV under Se-rich conditions), consistent with its p-type conduction. In w-MnSe, the Se antisite is lowest under Se-rich conditions, narrowly in the A-type order and clearly in the stripe order, and the Se vacancy is lowest under Mn-rich conditions. The Se vacancy has nearly the same formation energy in both polymorphs, whereas defects that change the number of Mn atoms differ by 0.4-1.1 eV, although DFT+$U$ places wurtzite below rock salt, contrary to experiment. A spin-degenerate stripe order lies 14 meV per formula unit below the altermagnetic A-type order of w-MnSe, and the formation energies shift between these orders by up to 0.24 eV, most for the Mn vacancy. Three of the four defects leave an uncompensated moment of 3-5 $\mu_\mathrm{B}$. In the A-type order, band unfolding shows that the sign-reversing splitting of the most strongly split band, about 230 meV and 3 eV below the valence-band maximum, keeps its peak height within the 8% scatter of the analysis at 3% defects, while points on its shoulders move by up to about 70 meV. Band-edge states are not resolved.

papers.title: Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-\Delta)^m u=u^{(n+2m)/(n-2m)}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0$. The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $\Delta^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-\Delta u$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.

papers.title: Identifying Chemically Coherent Stellar Families in the Galactic High-α Disk with Low-Resolution Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Identification of chemical substructures in the Galactic high-{\alpha} disk provides valuable insight into its formation history. In this work, we demonstrate the capability of low-resolution spectroscopy for this purpose by applying DBSCAN clustering to 87,275 red giants in the high-{\alpha} disk using 18 elemental abundances derived from LAMOST low-resolution spectra (R~1800). We assess the effectiveness of this approach by comparing the clustering results from the low-resolution data with those obtained by applying the same procedure to high-resolution survey abundances and to mock catalogs. These comparisons suggest that, despite the relatively large uncertainties in individual elemental abundances derived from low-resolution spectra, the astrophysical coherence among different elements provides sufficient information to identify chemically coherent families that may share similar enrichment histories without necessarily sharing a common birth environment. After scanning the parameter space of the DBSCAN procedure and merging the results from different parameter combinations, we identify 133 candidate chemical families containing 4,642 unique stars (5.3% of the high-{\alpha} disk sample). These families exhibit diverse multi-element abundance patterns, with particularly prominent differences in neutron-capture elements at nearly identical [Fe/H] values. These families therefore offer new constraints on the diversity of chemical enrichment pathways and on the assembly history of the high-{\alpha} disk.

papers.title: Stabilizing Vector Approximate Message Passing with Circuit-Designed Lag-Lead Damping
papers.abstract: Vector approximate message passing (VAMP) often fails to converge on ill-conditioned matrices, and its damping factor is tuned either manually or adaptively. Using the fact that VAMP iterations are the discretization of an electric circuit, we show that the denoiser and the likelihood act as nonlinear resistors, the Onsager correction is a mirror resistor and damping is a lag filter. This circuit gives a closed-form loop gain whose spectrum can predict when VAMP fails. Because a lag filter cannot isolate the oscillating modes, we add a lead capacitor whose design often results in a negative capacitance. Across a wide range of condition numbers, our proposed damping strategy achieves a higher convergence rate than adaptive damping and Anderson acceleration at a lower mean iteration cost. On ill-conditioned multipath channels, across ranks and sparsity levels, it also converges more reliably than existing damping baselines.

papers.title: Power Mean, Karcher Mean, and Log-Euclidean Mean on Positive Constant Upper Triangular Matrices
papers.abstract: We study weighted power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means on the Lie group CP_n of real upper triangular matrices with a constant positive diagonal. Building on the general triangular-group theory, we use the central decomposition CP_n \cong \mathbb R_+ -by-UP_n to separate the scalar power mean from a unipotent mean with reweighted coefficients. We prove that the power mean extends real-analytically through order zero, where it equals the Karcher mean. We establish exterior-power covariance for the Karcher and log-Euclidean means, and tensor-product identities for all three means, distinguishing product weights from paired inputs. Finite nilpotent functional calculus yields concise formulas on CP_2 and CP_3, where the Karcher and log-Euclidean means coincide. In dimension four, their difference is exactly a central cubic commutator, giving a necessary and sufficient equality criterion and an explicit counterexample. In every dimension, the same commutator is the leading term of their small-dispersion difference.

papers.title: Breathers across the Focusing-to-Defocusing Transition: From Diffraction-Like Dynamics to Talbot Carpets
papers.abstract: We experimentally investigate fundamental unstable breather wave groups propagating across the transition from focusing to defocusing regimes. In hydrodynamics, this transition is realized through a rapid reduction in water depth over a short spatial interval. We demonstrate that the time-periodic Akhmediev breather develops a Talbot-like recurrence pattern in the defocusing regime, although only its initial stages are experimentally accessible. In contrast, the Peregrine breather exhibits qualitatively different behavior, characterized by oscillatory envelope dynamics. These oscillations can be understood as a purely linear phenomenon arising within the nonlinear Schrödinger framework when dispersion dominates over nonlinearity, as further confirmed by numerical simulations over extended propagation distances. The experimental observations agree closely with finite-depth nonlinear Schrödinger predictions across regimes with substantially different relative strengths of dispersion and nonlinearity. Our findings reveal a temporal analogue of diffraction and provide a foundation for exploring focusing-to-defocusing transitions in other nonlinear dispersive media.

papers.title: The splitting type of jet bundles on the projective line
papers.abstract: Given a vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on a smooth variety X, one can associate to it its jet bundles, or bundles of principal parts. These bundles encode the Taylor expansions of local sections of $\mathcal{E}$ and arise naturally in the study of differential operators. When $X=\mathbb{P}^1$ is the projective line, jet bundles decompose as direct sums of line bundles, making it natural to study their splitting types. The splitting type is well understood in characteristic zero, but exhibits subtler behavior in positive characteristic. Our goal is to give a complete answer in every positive characteristic, and in particular to provide a characterization of semistability for jet bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$. We also determine their extremal summands and give applications to differential operators and formulas for cohomology of line bundles on infinitesimal thickenings of the diagonal.

papers.title: Optimal asymptotic pure-state conversion under thermal operations
papers.abstract: Quantum thermodynamics seeks to characterize possible state transformations under thermodynamic constraints in microscopic quantum systems. In the fully quantum regime, however, quantum coherence imposes various restrictions on state conversions, and a complete characterization of state convertibility has remained open. Here we resolve this problem for asymptotic conversions between pure states. Specifically, we show that asymptotic convertibility is fully determined by the free-energy and energy-variance ratios. Our result reveals how genuinely quantum effects quantitatively constrain state conversions in quantum thermodynamics.

papers.title: Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
papers.abstract: We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.

papers.title: Portfolio-aware scenario transfer of reserve movements: evidence from Lloyd's syndicates
papers.abstract: A claims-development movement on one portfolio may not transfer directly as a stress to another size. We estimate how to transfer such scenarios between portfolio sizes, using 632 syndicate-years from 117 Lloyd's syndicates over 2015-2024. The measured movement is the change in gross claims estimates on selected older underwriting cohorts, divided by opening gross claims outstanding plus reserves taken on in the year whose development it includes; it is not a pure measure of opening-reserve deterioration. Its dispersion falls materially with reserve size, and a size-based scale predicts held-out syndicates far better than a single market scale. But the transferred upper tail understates the smallest books: in the smallest reserve-size quartile, six of 158 held-out observations exceeded the transferred 99.5th percentile, against 0.79 expected, from three syndicates. Square-root scaling has descriptively lower held-out pinball loss at 99% and 99.5%, though more misses among the largest books. For a GBP 500m portfolio the transferred empirical 99.5th percentile is 0.34 of reserves (95% credible interval, conditional on the fitted model, 0.23-0.52), against 0.67 in the raw market pool. Both are Syndicate 5820's 2016 movement. The contribution is inspectable scenario comparability, not a calibrated capital quantile or a next-year forecast.

papers.title: Evaporation-induced colloidal diffusiophoresis in electrolyte solutions
papers.abstract: Non-volatile solutes accumulate near a receding drying front, generating concentration gradients that can drive directional colloidal transport by diffusiophoresis. This dynamic spatial arrangement of colloidal particles could affect the microstructure and macroscopic properties of the dried film. Here, we combine experiments and theory to investigate polystyrene particles suspended in electrolyte solutions drying within a capillary tube. By varying the electrolyte composition and ambient relative humidity, we show that evaporation-induced ion gradients drive particles toward the liquid-gas interface and enhance interfacial accumulation, whereas slower drying at higher humidity weakens the gradient and particle migration. We use the heat balance integral method to predict the transient solute field for a receding interface and couple it to particle transport to capture the observed particle trajectories and accumulation trends. These results identify background electrolytes and drying rate as coupled controls on particle distribution and provide a predictive framework to optimize formulation and processing parameters for manufacturing slurry-based materials, such as battery electrodes and turbine coatings.

papers.title: Joint Approximation and the Mixed-Prime Character Group
papers.abstract: For the integer metric defined by the square denominators of two distinct primes, we prove simultaneous approximation to zero in one prime metric and to any prescribed integer in the other. A normalized convolution argument gives a uniform central spectral bound. Random relative translations of smooth weights produce an exact positive cas cade; Fourier positivity places every normalized finer convolution below its value at zero. A far-field recursion, the growth of merged square powers, and a two-term logarithmic-form estimate give summable fac tor bounds. Consequently, for every fixed pair of distinct primes p,q, the mixed continuous character group is Z[1/(pq)]/Z: no irrational pa rameter is continuous. The mixed completion is the product of the one-prime completions. For each fixed pair this also gives a compati ble rational join and a strictly finer compatible join of the associated real TVG topologies, with the same prescribed real character group. Exact witness search terminates at every strict precision and integer target. We retain the structural, density, divisibility, sequence and finite-certificate results leading to this proof. The existence argument does not give practical witness-size or runtime bounds, and it does not assume independence or equidistribution of the two digit systems. Se lected abstract components have been checked using Lean and Mathlib; the complete analytic argument has not been formalized. The corre sponding problem for three or more primes remains separate.

papers.title: Disjointness preserving operators on Köthe-Banach spaces
papers.abstract: A well-known result of Abramovich says that if $E$, $F$ are rearrangement invariant Banach spaces on a finite atomless measure space such that $E$ has an absolutely continuous norm and $E\not\subseteq F$, then there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$. We obtain an analogue of this result in the setting of general Köthe-Banach spaces. Specifically, we identify a sufficient condition on Köthe-Banach spaces $E$, $F$ on finite atomless measure spaces that implies that there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$. Consequently, by a representation theorem for regular operators due to O.~Maslyuchenko, Mykhaylyuk and the second named author, this condition implies that every regular linear operator $T \colon E\to F$ is narrow. As an application, we obtain that if $1\le \max\{p_1,p_2\}< \min\{ r_1, r_2\}\le \infty$, then every regular linear operator $T \colon L_{p_1}(L_{p_2}) \to L_{r_1}(L_{r_2})$ is narrow. The latter may be seen as an analogue of the classical Pitt compactness theorem.

papers.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
papers.abstract: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.

papers.title: A Poincare-Einstein Liouville Theorem and the Yamabe Invariant of Lens Spaces
papers.abstract: Schoen conjectured that the Yamabe invariant of every lens space is achieved by the round metric. A proof of this conjecture is presented for all lens spaces, together with rigidity: equality is only achieved for the round class. The key step is to show that every $\mathbb Z_p$-invariant Yamabe-positive conformal class on $S^3$ admits a $\mathbb Z_p$-equivariant Poincaré-Einstein filling. The distance function from a fixed point of the filling then gives an invariant test function with Yamabe quotient at most $\sigma(S^3)$, which descends to the lens space. The proof of the main theorem was generated by AI (ChatGPT Astra, September 2026); this is mainly a learning note of the AI generated proof.

papers.title: System noise temperature measurements of a 19-element phased array feed
papers.abstract: We present multi-epoch system noise temperature measurements of a 19 element hexagonal room-temperature phased array feed (PAF) using a modified Y-factor method. A Python-based pipeline with iterative channel calibration and maxSNR beam forming is developed to do data reduction, and a covariance-based decomposition scheme is proposed to extract mutual coupling noise temperature Tmc. Long-term observations from March to June 2026 capture temporal receiver noise drift mainly induced by LNA temperature variations. Within the 1.37-1.47 GHz operating band, the measured beam equivalent system noise temperature of the PAF is about 73-89 K. The measured Tmc baseline ranges from about 2 K to 8 K, while under thermal loading, the resonant peak of Tmc can increase to more than 20 K. The baseline of Tmc is consistent with the S-parameter mea surements, which show the Tmc of the full array ranges less than 10.7 K. The baseline fluctuation of Tmc most likely arises from the superposition of thermal and non-thermal components of the spatial electromagnetic fields. A detachable stainless steel shield is deployed to quantify sidelobe spillover noise, and comparative tests show unshielded en vironmental interference increases receiver noise temperature by over 60 K. The proposed measurements and data processing framework provides a practical reference for noise per formance characterization of ground-based radio telescope PAF prototypes.

papers.title: Equatorial Periodic Orbits and Gravitational Wave Signatures in Weyl Geometric Gravity Black Holes
Mixed-dimensional topological charge compensation beyond Weyl-node pairing
papers.abstract: The Nielsen-Ninomiya no-go theorem requires the total topological charge ($C$) in a periodic Brillouin zone to vanish, conventionally leading to opposite-chirality pairs of Weyl points (WPs). A charged nodal surface (NS) provides an alternative mechanism for compensating a same-chirality Weyl pair, yet the general symmetry constraints governing this configuration and its electronic realization remain unexplored. Here, by an exhaustive analysis of all 1651 magnetic space groups (MSGs), with and without spin-orbit coupling, we identify only 13 type-II MSGs that permit the realization of a minimal unpaired mixed-dimensional configuration comprising a single $|C|=2$ NS and two same-chirality $|C|=1$ WPs. Guided by this symmetry framework, we identify the chiral boron allotrope THC-B$_{30}$ as the first electronic realization of this unconventional topology. First-principles calculations reveal only two WPs with $C=-1$ and one NS with $C=+2$, satisfying global topological charge neutrality and exhibiting unconventional Fermi arcs connecting the WP and NS projections. Moreover, strain-induced topological phase transitions redistribute topological charge among distinct band-degeneracy manifolds. Our findings establish a symmetry-guided route to realizing same-chirality Weyl pairs through mixed-dimensional charge compensation beyond conventional Weyl-node pairing.

papers.title: The Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes
papers.abstract: In recent years, the Schur products of linear codes have been extensively studied due to their favorable applications in cryptography. In this paper, we aim to study the parameters of the Schur products of some nonbinary narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes. Let $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ be two narrow-sense antiprimitive BCH codes with designed distances $\delta_{1}$ and $\delta_{2}$, respectively, where $2\le \delta_{1},\delta_{2}\le n$. Let $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2$ be the Schur product of $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$. We present some necessary and sufficient conditions for $\mathcal{C}_1\star\mathcal{C}_2\ne\mathbb{F}_q^n$ by applying some constraints to $\delta_{1}$ and $\delta_{2}$. Furthermore, we determine the dimensions of these products and lower bounds on their minimum distance. Several linear codes with best known parameters are found.

papers.title: Centralizers of elliptic univalent self-maps and the embeddability problem in the unit disc
papers.abstract: Let $\phi$ be an elliptic univalent self-map of the unit disc in the complex plane that is not an automorphism, with multiplier $0<|\lambda|<1$ at its Denjoy--Wolff point. The simultaneous Schröder linearization of maps commuting with $\phi$ is classical. Using this linearization, we identify its univalent centralizer with the multiplicative semigroup of scalars that preserve the Koenigs domain, and investigate how the geometry of this semigroup controls continuous-time embeddings. We show that the identity is a non-isolated point of the centralizer precisely when the centralizer contains a non-trivial continuous one-parameter semigroup; such a semigroup need not contain $\phi$. For each logarithmic branch $\mu_k=-\mathrm{Log}\lambda+2\pi i k$, we establish a local sector alternative that characterizes the existence of an embedding with spectral value $\mu_k$. We prove that the set of admissible branch indices is either empty, a finite interval of integers, or all of $\mathbb{Z}$, and give examples realizing all three possibilities. Finally, we describe the full holomorphic centralizer, including the constant map with value equal to the Denjoy--Wolff point.

papers.title: Bounds on Negligible Thresholds in Group Cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field, $K/F$ a field extension with $\Gamma_K:=\text{Gal}(K_\text{sep}/K)$, $G$ a finite group, $j:\Gamma_K\rightarrow G$ a continuous group homomorphism, and $M$ an abelian group. There is an induced map of profinite cohomology $j^*:H^n (G;M)\rightarrow H^n (K;M)=:H^n (\Gamma_K;M)$. An element $u\in H^n (G;M)$ is negligible over $F$ if $j^* (u)=0$ for all such $j$ and field extensions $K/F$. The subset of negligible elements forms a subgroup $H^n (G;M)_{\text{neg},F}\subseteq H^n (G;M)$. The negligible threshold $\text{nthres}^G_F (M)$ is the smallest $N\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 0}\cup\{\infty\}$ such that $H^n (G;M)_{\text{neg},F}=H^n (G;M)$ for all $n\geq N$. In this paper, we first establish some general bounds for negligible thresholds of arbitrary triples $(G,M,F)$ consisting of a finite group $G$, trivial $G$-module $M$, and field $F$. We then compute the negligible thresholds of an arbitrary group when $F$ is a field of characteristic $p$ and $M=\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z}$. Continuing in the characteristic $p$ setting, we compute these thresholds for $G$ a $p$-group and $M=\mathbb{Z}$, and we compute the thresholds for $G=\mathbb{Z}/\ell\mathbb{Z},M=\mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$ for integers $s,\ell\in\mathbb{N}_{>1}$ satisfying certain number theoretic conditions. For fields containing sufficiently many roots of unity, we show that the negligible threshold of odd exponent finitely-generated trivial $G$-modules is finite. For $G$-modules of the form $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, $p$ an odd prime, we compute an explicit upper bound for the negligible threshold in terms of $p$ and $|G|$. We conclude by providing explicit computations of the negligible thresholds of elementary abelian $p$-groups with mod-$p$ coefficients, negligible thresholds of cyclic groups, and bounds on mod-$p$ negligible thresholds of general finite abelian $p$-groups.

papers.title: Supervised Factor-Augmented Matrix Regression with Weak Factors
papers.abstract: We develop a supervised factor-augmented matrix regression framework for high-dimensional analysis with weak factors. When factor loadings are concentrated on unknown subsets of rows and columns, conventional full-matrix factor extraction may suffer substantial signal dilution, with weakness in one matrix dimension propagating to estimation in the other. We characterize this two-way weak-loading phenomenon for both \(\alpha\)-PCA and projected estimators and show that their loading and factor estimates may deteriorate under weak signals. To address this problem, we propose a sequential response-guided screening procedure that identifies informative rows and columns prior to factor extraction. We establish exact support recovery and show that post-screening factor re-estimation converts the weak-loading problem into a pervasive one relative to the retained dimensions, yielding sharper convergence rates under substantially weaker dimensional growth conditions and consistent factor-number determination.
