We further establish asymptotic distributions for both unrestricted and bilinear regression estimators based on the estimated matrix factors. Simulations demonstrate substantial improvements in support recovery and factor estimation under weak signals. We illustrate the gains obtained by the response-guided factor construction with two empirical applications.

papers.title: Local distinguishability of five five-partite orthogonal product states
Advection-aligned block Vecchia inference for spatio-temporal Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: Vecchia approximations enable scalable likelihood-based inference for large Gaussian process models, but their accuracy depends on the choice of conditioning sets. For spatio-temporal processes with advection, target-centered conditioning can omit informative past observations. Motivated by total column ozone observations from the Geostationary Environment Monitoring Spectrometer (GEMS), we propose a data-driven, advection-aligned block Vecchia approximation that incorporates estimated transport direction into temporal conditioning geometry. Observation locations need not lie on a regular grid. An initial advection vector is estimated from the data and used once to select transport-aligned past-time conditioning blocks. The resulting graph is held fixed during optimization, while covariance and advection parameters remain free to vary. This separates neighbor selection from covariance estimation, avoids repeated parameter-dependent neighbor searches, and provides an interpretable connection between conditioning geometry and estimated transport. Batched graphics processing unit (GPU) operations evaluate the likelihood and its gradients. In a matched comparison of daily GEMS datasets from July 2024 and July 2025, advection-aligned conditioning attained a lower fitted Vecchia negative log-likelihood than target-centered conditioning on 53 of 61 days. In six Matérn simulation scenarios with 120 matched eight-hour fields each, advection-aligned conditioning reduced advection-vector root mean squared error relative to target-centered conditioning at the same conditioning-block budget, with the largest reduction under strong transport.

papers.title: Ordered Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) stabilizes policy updates by clipping the importance ratio between the new policy and the data-collecting policy. The standard rule uses one fixed clipping range for all samples. While this choice offers simplicity and effectiveness, it fails to distinguish statistically harmful extreme ratio values from large, yet tolerable changes. We study how to adapt the clipping radius to the reliability of the induced importance ratio distribution. Our case study demonstrates that reliable updates require controlling these extreme ratios, rather than merely verifying that individual ratios fall within a fixed interval. Motivated by this observation, we propose Ordered Policy Optimization (\textsc{OPO}). In each minibatch, \textsc{OPO} sorts the importance ratios, selects the extreme ratios that potentially have the largest effect on the update, and assigns them adaptive sample-wise radii instead of using the fixed clipping radius. These radii are derived from a prescribed tail profile, which specifies desired target values for the selected extreme ratios. The resulting objective remains first-order and requires only minibatch sorting and a modified policy loss. Experiments conducted on MuJoCo and Atari benchmarks demonstrate that this simple modification achieves strong performance relative to established baselines.

papers.title: AdS${}_3$/BCFT${}_2$ correspondence and 't Hooft anomaly of U(1) symmetry
A stochastic propagation method for large-scale phonon calculations
papers.abstract: Large-scale phonon calculations for structurally complex materials are limited by the cubic cost of full diagonalization. We extend the stochastic propagation method (sPM) from electronic systems to lattice dynamics for estimating phonon frequencies, constructing vibrational densities of states, and reconstructing selected phonon polarization vectors by propagating random initial vectors under the dynamical matrix. For finite-range interactions, the leading propagation cost scales linearly with atom number at fixed sampling and propagation parameters. Our error analysis shows that, for nondegenerate modes that are spectrally resolved and have nonzero frequency in the small-error regime, extending propagation yields faster asymptotic reduction of frequency-estimation errors than increasing the number of random initial states alone. Comparisons with direct diagonalization validate the spectral estimates and a selected polarization vector. Convergence tests support the predicted scaling of frequency errors for selected resolved modes.

papers.title: Tidal Braking Does Not Dominate Open-Cluster Slow Rotators
papers.abstract: Extended main-sequence turn-offs (eMSTOs) observed in open clusters younger than $2~\mathrm{Gyr}$ are commonly attributed to a spread in stellar rotation rates. Tidal synchronization in close binary systems has been proposed as a possible mechanism for producing slowly rotating stars. To test this hypothesis, we measured the radial-velocity (RV) dispersions of slow-rotator samples associated with the eMSTOs of eight open clusters using ESO VLT/GIRAFFE and SALT/RSS spectroscopy. We extended the analysis to 40 open clusters using Gaia DR3 RV measurements. The observed cluster RV dispersions are generally substantially smaller than those predicted for binary populations dominated by close systems with orbital periods for which tidal synchronization is expected to be effective. In particular, all 40 clusters in the Gaia sample have RV dispersions below the prediction of the $P=10$ d binary-population model. These results suggest that close, tidally synchronized binaries are unlikely to be the dominant origin of slow-rotator populations in young and intermediate-age open clusters, although a contribution from undetected or wider binary systems cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Optimal Separations Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity under Permutation Symmetry
On the Incompleteness of do-calculus for Universal Identifiability
papers.abstract: We study the problem of causal effect identification from an arbitrary set of observational and/or interventional distributions, which we call Universal Identifiability (uID). The uID problem generalizes existing classical identifiability (ID) and general identifiability (gID) problems, which considered the identification problem from either mere observational distributions or a specific type of interventional distributions. Prior research has established graphical criteria to determine when a causal effect is identifiable in ID and gID problems. Moreover, algorithms that leverage do-calculus and basic probability manipulations have been proposed to compute these effects. Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. Despite these well-established results, a formal definition of what it means for the do-calculus to be complete does not exist. We propose a rigorous formalization for the completeness of the do-calculus and show that the completeness results in previous work remain valid. However, for more general problems, such as uID, the rules of do-calculus are no longer complete. This is perhaps the reason why the uID problem has remained open thus far.

papers.title: Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_{\beta}$ to $A^p_{\alpha}$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_{\alpha}]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_{\beta}$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_{\beta}$. Moreover, $A^q_{\beta} \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_{\alpha}]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_{\beta}$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_{\alpha}]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_{\gamma}] \subset [T_{g},A^p_{\alpha}]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

papers.title: Time- and phase-resolved emulation of sign-selective counterdiabatic dynamics in a superconducting qutrit
Task-Contribution Dynamics of Adam in Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Slow-Manifold Analysis and Gradient Modulation
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often suffer from imbalanced optimization of competing loss components, particularly when approximating solutions with high-frequency or multiscale features. Although existing balancing strategies have proven effective in alleviating this difficulty, the mechanisms governing the evolution of individual task contributions to Adam's parameter updates remain insufficiently understood. We introduce task-wise indicators to characterize this evolution and identify three distinct training regimes: smooth variation, intermittent spikes, and persistent oscillations. Focusing on the early smooth regime, we combine discrete-time analysis with a continuous-time singular perturbation framework under the full-batch setting and the parameter regime $(1-\beta_2)/(1-\beta_1)\ll1$. A first-order approximation of the locally attracting slow manifold reveals two factors governing the step-to-step redistribution of task contributions: curvature-related alignment disparities and differences in the coordinatewise distributions of preconditioned task gradients. Both factors involve Adam's shared second-moment estimate. Inspired by AdaTask, we propose Gradient-Modulated Adam (GMAdam), which modulates incoming task gradients using task-specific second-moment estimates. Numerical experiments on high-frequency Poisson and wave equations, the Allen-Cahn equation, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity flow ($Re=100,400$) demonstrate consistent improvements in predictive accuracy over AdaTask at comparable computational cost.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: The recently proposed Score-Repellent Monte Carlo (SRMC) method improves MCMC sampling by tilting the target density $\pi$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the factor $\exp(-\alpha\,\theta_n^\top s(x))$, where the score function $s(x) = \nabla_x \log \pi(x)$, and $\theta_n$ is the score average from past samples. However, a single scalar repellence strength $\alpha\ge0$ cannot handle both the steep and the flat directions in anisotropic energy landscapes at once. We introduce \emph{Geometry-Aware SRMC} (GA-SRMC), which generalizes the Euclidean alignment to $\theta^\top M s(x)$ for any symmetric positive-definite matrix $M$. A stochastic-approximation central limit theorem under a trace constraint on $M$ identifies the trace-normalized inverse Fisher $M_{\rm opt}\propto S^{-1}$ as the unique minimizer of the worst-direction covariance bound, elevating the Fisher information $S=\text{Cov}_\pi(s,s)$ from a proposal-side preconditioner (e.g., FisherMALA, natural gradient) to the bound-optimal repulsion-side matrix, with a single online estimate $\widehat S_n$ serving both roles at no additional computational cost. The full-Fisher online metric $M_n$ converges almost surely to $M_{\rm opt}$ and satisfies a CLT, providing a theoretical guarantee for the online implementation of the GA-SRMC framework. On an $8$-target simulation spanning the condition number $\kappa\in[1.3,100]$ and dimension $d\in[2,785]$, GA-SRMC dominates SRMC in ESS by $\boldsymbol{4.3\times}$ on anisotropic Gaussian ($\kappa=100$) and $\boldsymbol{6.8\times}$ on MNIST under the MALA baseline, by $\boldsymbol{16\text{--}32\%}$ on three well-conditioned logistic-regression posteriors, and by up to $\boldsymbol{+48\%}$ under FisherMALA; gains peak on the most anisotropic targets, and posterior-mean MSE is lower than with SRMC in all $16$ full-Fisher implementations.

papers.title: Shared Lookups and Lazy Residues: Fewer Toffoli Gates for Factoring RSA-2048
Quantum Fluctuations in Noether's Theorem
Snow Changes Drought Characterization but Not Drought Predictability: A Leakage-Free Multiscale Study in Ohio
papers.abstract: We examine whether accounting for snow accumulation and melt, which precipitation-based drought indices ignore, changes drought characterization and one-month-ahead drought forecasting at three stations in Ohio, USA (1953--2026). The Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) is compared with the Standardized Snow Melt and Rain Index (SMRI), and both are decomposed with the Haar maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform. Nonlinear autoregressive networks without (NAR) and with (NARX) wavelet inputs are compared over 100 paired repetitions in a leakage-free design (past-only wavelet inputs, untouched test period), together with persistence, climatology, and linear autoregressive benchmarks. Snow changes the 3-month index mainly from December to May (mean absolute SMRI--SPI differences of up to 0.17--0.28). These differences are attributable to the snow-adjusted input rather than to the fitted distribution, are robust to the snow-model parameters, and change the drought classification of 21--32\% of the December--May drought months. Wavelet inputs reduce NARX error relative to NAR by 6--10\% for the 3-month indices in 92--100\% of the repetitions, but not for the 6-month indices. A linear autoregression with 7--12 lags is at least as accurate as two-lag NARX for every series, and networks given six lags gain at most 4.5\% from the wavelet inputs and only match the autoregression. The forecast gain therefore reflects the memory of the accumulated index rather than multiscale information, and it is similar for the SPI and the SMRI. Snow matters for drought monitoring in winter and spring, but not for one-month predictability.

papers.title: A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic
papers.abstract: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations, and Reggio proved the theorem equivalent to the Beth definability property of an infinitary equational logic. We extend both results beyond compactness: on every separable metric space, and in particular on every Polish space, every bounded uniformly continuous function is a uniform limit of functions built from countably many bounded separating functions by the connectives of infinitary real-valued logic, and an approximate Beth property of this logic is equivalent to the new theorem. The extension rests on a rule of syntax, which admits a countable supremum when its terms share an a priori bound and thereby makes the sentences define exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and on a model existence game that does the work of compactness in the proof of interpolation.

papers.title: Reflections of Nichols algebras in braided monoidal categories
papers.abstract: Let $\C$ be an essentially small abelian rigid braided monoidal category. We prove a reflection theorem for Nichols algebras in $\Ind(\C)$ and show that tuples admitting all reflections define connected semi-Cartan graphs. As applications, we prove that a finite Nichols algebra has a generating object of length at most one in $PSU(2)_k$ for odd $k\ge3$, in $SU(2)_{4m}$ for $m\ge1$, and in the representation categories of the Virasoro minimal models $\mathcal M(2,p)$ for odd $p\ge5$. In all three families, we prove that every finite pre-Nichols algebra is a Nichols algebra.

papers.title: Spiral momentum spectra and spin asymmetry in vacuum pair production driven by phase-modulated elliptically polarized electric fields
papers.abstract: We study vacuum electron--positron pair production in phase-modulated elliptically polarized electric fields using the quantum kinetic equations. We analyze how the modulation amplitude, frequency, ellipticity, and modulation form affect the spin-resolved momentum spectra and the spin asymmetry. Cosine-type modulation can deform ring-shaped momentum distributions into spiral patterns. This deformation depends nonmonotonically on the modulation amplitude and frequency and is most pronounced for circular polarization. In the transverse momentum plane, the spin-resolved yields favor the spin channel along the direction of field handedness. Reversing the field handedness would reverse the favored channel while leaving the total yield unchanged. Sine-type modulation preserves ring-shaped and mirror-symmetric spectra approximately, however, it leads to a stronger dependence of the spin asymmetry on the modulation amplitude than cosine-type modulation does. These results show that phase modulation and ellipticity can control the momentum spectra patterns in vacuum pair production. Moreover, phase modulation can also affect the degree of spin asymmetry.

papers.title: Empirical approximation of $L_p$ norms for $p\in (2, \infty)$
papers.abstract: For $p>2$ and an $N$-dimensional subspace $X\subset L_\infty(\mu)$ satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that $m\ge C(p)KN \bigl(\varepsilon^{-p} +\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(2N)\bigr)$ independent samples $\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^m$ with distribution $\mu$ satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c(p)\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This gives the optimal sample-size order $N\log_2 N$ for independent random sampling with fixed $K$, $p$, and $\varepsilon$. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of $p$-convex norms.

papers.title: A Real-Space Framework for the Bare and Interacting Longitudinal Susceptibility of Solids
papers.abstract: We present an implementation of the bare and interacting longitudinal susceptibility in a full-potential linear muffin-tin orbital code. The bare susceptibility is built in real space from Matsubara sums of Kohn-Sham Green's functions and is resolved by site, spin and orbital degrees of freedom; the spin and charge susceptibilities follow from a Dyson equation, with an on-site exchange-correlation kernel. After testing the solver on the Stoner-like instability of bcc Fe, we apply it to four density-wave materials. The bare susceptibility peaks at H in bcc Cr, where the nonmagnetic state is close to a Stoner instability, and at the stripe vector M in FeSe. In LaTe3 the response of the Te nets peaks close to the observed charge-density-wave vector, at its image in the neighbouring Brillouin zone; which of the two equivalent vectors carries the response is set by the phases of the sites in the cell. In 2H-NbSe2 the response is weakly modulated, and the observed vector lies on the flank of a broad maximum, consistent with the known importance of electron-phonon coupling there. Antiferromagnetic order reduces the bare longitudinal response at the ordering vector by ~8% in Cr and about half in FeSe. The orbital decomposition of the bare susceptibility shows which orbitals contribute the most for the nearest-neighbor bonds.

papers.title: Slice Regular Capacity and Rational Approximation
papers.abstract: Approximation theory in the complex plane is a well established area of mathematical research, with extensive contributions documented in the literature, notably through the classical results of Weierstrass, Runge, Mergelyan, and Vitushkin. Approximation theory in quaternionic settings, particularly rational approximation on compact sets, which studies when slice regular functions can be uniformly approximated by rational functions, is one of the recent areas of interest in quaternionic rational approximation theory (See [6,13]). In this paper, we discuss Vitushkin approximation theorem in the quaternionic setting by using the quaternionic analogue of analytic capacity and also we establish Davies modified Vitushkin scheme in quaternionic setting. We also discuss quaternionic analogue of $\gamma_{+}$- capacity and Cauchy capacity and the remarkable results of Tolsa [35] and Younsi [45] related to these capacities in complex plane setting.

papers.title: Predicting Continuum Emission in Massive Star-Forming Regions with Embedded HII Regions - Dust, Free-Free, and Anomalous Microwave Emission with POLARIS
papers.abstract: Context: HII regions are a key stage of massive star formation, where ionizing radiation reshapes the interstellar medium. Their continuum spectra trace thermal dust, free-free emission, and anomalous microwave emission (AME). Aims: We investigate how these components evolve as an HII region expands and correlate with gas and electron column densities across spatial scales. Methods: We post-process RAMSES radiation-magnetohydrodynamical simulations of a $10^4 M_\odot$ cloud with POLARIS. The model includes grain charging, rotational excitation and damping, radiative torques, rotational disruption, and emission from dust, ionized gas, and nano-composite grains. We compute maps and SEDs for six snapshots over $1-10^4$ GHz and analyze multi-scale correlations. Results: Ionized emission evolves from a compact, optically thick HII region to an extended, optically thin structure. Around 15 GHz, free-free emission changes from a $\nu^2$ to a $\nu^{-0.1}$ spectral regime as optical depth decreases, and increasingly traces electron column density. The thermal dust peak shifts from mid- to far-infrared as colder material contributes, while dust emission remains strongly correlated with total gas column density. AME peaks at 26-37 GHz and shows scale-dependent correlations with gas and electron distributions. Rotational disruption is the main dust-destruction mechanism affecting mid-infrared emission and the high-frequency AME tail. Conclusions: These continuum components provide complementary, scale-dependent diagnostics of stellar feedback. Self-consistent multi-frequency modeling is essential for interpreting surveys of star-forming clouds.

papers.title: A counterexample to Manin's Conjecture for almost Fano varieties
papers.abstract: We give an example of a smooth rational threefold over a number field with a big anticanonical divisor that does not satisfy the thin set version of Manin's Conjecture. In particular, Manin's Conjecture does not hold for rationally connected almost Fano varieties.

papers.title: Generalized Edge Ideals and Regularity Offset of Graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized edge ideals by assigning pairwise coprime monomials, instead of variables, to the vertices of a graph. We use the lcm-lattice to show that the multigraded Betti numbers and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the quotient by a generalized edge ideal agree with the Betti numbers and resolution regularity of the quotient by an ordinary edge ideal in a non-standard Z-grading. We define the regularity offset as a measurement of the difference between the regularities of the quotients by a generalized edge ideal and its ordinary counterpart, and prove bounds for the regularity offset. We compute the regularity offset for co-chordal graphs and paths, and derive a formula for the regularity offset of forests. We also derive a graph-theoretic criterion for when a forest's regularity offset is always zero, or equivalently, its top-level Betti number is nonzero.

papers.title: On nonlocal geometric rigidity estimates in bounded uniform domains
papers.abstract: We prove fractional geometric rigidity estimates and fractional Korn's first inequalities with general singular weights in bounded uniform domains in $\mathbb R^n.$ The classical choice of the energy well $SO(n)$ for the geometric rigidity estimate fails due to the lack of a notion of orientation for Lebesgue fields. The remedy is to choose $O(n)$ as the energy well. Due to the recently developed theory of local-to-nonlocal passage of rigidity estimates developed by the first author, both estimates reduce to the analogous local estimates on the cube, which we prove in several steps by compactness and linearization arguments.

papers.title: KAM theory for quasi-periodic equilibrium of generalized Frenkel-Kontorova model in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$
papers.abstract: We extend the KAM theory for one dimensional Frenkel-Kontorova model to multidimensional case in quasi-periodic media. By using the quasi-Newton method, we reduce the linearized operator with quasi-periodic coefficient in the Nash-Moser iteration to the composition of two diagonal operators and a near-identity operator, such that the small divisor problem can be overcome by imposing the simultaneous Diophantine condition. In contrast, we also discuss the application of Craig-Wayne-Bourgain method to the quasi-periodic equilibrium problem.

papers.title: Modeling of the X-ray Flux and Polarization Energy Spectra of Black Hole X-Ray Binaries with the KerrC Code
papers.abstract: In this chapter, we introduce the kerrC model, an advanced framework designed for the analysis of combined spectral and polarimetric X-ray emission from black hole systems. The model is built upon an extensive dataset of ray-tracing Monte Carlo simulations that compute the radiative transfer of X-rays in the strongly curved spacetime near the event horizon of a Kerr black hole. These simulations incorporate thermal seed emission from a geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk, along with the subsequent Comptonization processes within a hot corona of variable geometry and physical properties. Crucially, the reflection of both primary disk and Comptonized photons is treated self-consistently utilizing the xillver reflection tables, and the polarization 4-vectors of the photons are rigorously transported throughout the simulation to preserve full polarization information. The code tracks photons forward in time, allowing for multiple photon scatterings in the corona and off the accretion disk. We detail the underlying mechanics of the ray-tracing simulations and the fitting models, and discuss the applications of kerrC in leveraging X-ray polarization observations to constrain black hole spin and coronal geometry.

papers.title: Limits of Lorenz number estimation from the temperature-dependent Seebeck coefficient
papers.abstract: Separating electronic and lattice thermal conductivity often relies on a Lorenz number estimated from the Seebeck coefficient using an assumed band and scattering model. We ask how much information about the Lorenz number comes from temperature-dependent Seebeck coefficients rather than the assumed model. We formulate compatible minimum and maximum Lorenz numbers as linear programs in a fixed finite spectral representation, assuming known chemical potentials and a common energy dependence across observation temperatures for each candidate spectrum. Reference Seebeck coefficients are generated by single-band and same-sign two-band models. Increasing the prescribed observations from one to five temperatures reduces the Lorenz interval widths by approximately 97.6% and 97.8%, respectively. Nevertheless, the single-band example retains an attained interval of approximately $[1.46453,2.37037]\times10^{-8}$ W $\Omega$ K$^{-2}$ at 400 K. Exact electrical conductivity values do not narrow these ranges when spectral amplitudes can vary independently with temperature. Thus, even exact Seebeck coefficients and electrical conductivities at all five temperatures need not uniquely determine electronic thermal conductivity at 400 K. For the same single-band example, known ratios of spectral amplitudes across temperatures allow electrical conductivity values to confine all compatible Lorenz numbers to an enclosing interval less than 1% as wide as the five-temperature free-amplitude interval. Temperature-dependent Seebeck data strongly narrow the compatible range, while conductivity provides further spectral constraints when the temperature dependence of spectral amplitudes is independently restricted.

papers.title: A pipeline for identifying astrophysical signals and instrumental glitches in LISA data
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a space-based gravitational wave detector scheduled for launch in the 2030s by the European Space Agency. Operating in the 0.1 mHz to 0.1 Hz band, LISA will observe a variety of astrophysical sources including but not limited to supermassive black hole mergers, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and white dwarf binaries. LISA will yield new insights, including supermassive black hole formation, new tests of general relativity, population studies of white dwarfs and others. Like all interferometric gravitational wave detectors, LISA data is expected to contain non-astrophysical transients, commonly referred to as glitches. We introduce a two step pipeline that consists of a search algorithm for detecting potential transients in simulated LISA data followed by a machine learning model that classifies the detected transients as gravitational waves or instrumental glitches. This is important for MBHBs with very high masses (around $10^6\ M_{\odot}$) which are transients that could be morphologically similar to LISA glitches in the data. Initial results demonstrate a promising ability to classify detected events with an accuracy close to $98\%$. The pipeline also shows the ability to analyze a month of data in under 2 minutes on a laptop. This shows an eventual utility of our pipeline for enabling accurate rapid alerts from low latency searches. It could also support model selection in global-fit analyses by providing an initial summary of the location and type of individual signals. This paper also discusses challenges encountered during training, including limitations of the current framework.

papers.title: Simplicity of the three-point stress-tensor form factor beyond the planar limit
Reweighting for Transfer Classification: Exact Risk Conversion and Minimax Adaptation
papers.abstract: A source can make a training mixture easier to learn while making its accuracy less valuable for the target. We study how the training problem a source creates and the finite-sample error of learning it jointly determine target-risk guarantees under reweighting. For binary classification, for each pair of laws and each positive target weight, we derive the sharpest target excess hinge-risk bound implied by mixture excess alone, uniformly over clipped predictors. This exact conversion curve is determined by density-weighted local votes. A two-sample oracle inequality for weighted support vector machines supplies the mixture excess, and the composition becomes explicit for Gaussian kernels. On a tilted-boundary class, we establish the all-procedure minimax classification rate $[n+s_+^2/(m^{-1}+\tau^2)]^{-1}$ in the transferable strength $s_+$ and the tilt $\tau$, separating source sampling uncertainty ($m^{-1}$) from relation uncertainty ($\tau^2$). A target-checked Gaussian-SVM selector adapts to unknown $s_+$ and $\tau$ up to a logarithmic factor for fixed dimension, and retains the target-only rate up to the same factor against arbitrary independent sources under the stated target model. On a separate smooth opposition class, the minimax risk within the family of exact Gaussian SVMs fitted to the original labels with nonnegative weights is exponentially larger than the unrestricted minimax risk whenever the target sample is at most half the source sample, despite arbitrary data-dependent weighting and tuning. The value of a source thus depends on the training problem it creates, on what accuracy there means for the target, and on whether the permitted use of the source can implement the needed correction.

papers.title: Twist-3 and flavor-singlet contributions to $γγ\toπ^{0}η^{(\prime)}$ and $η^{(\prime)}η^{(\prime)}$ in $k_{T}$ factorization
papers.abstract: We study two-photon production of the pseudoscalar pairs $\pi^{0}\eta$, $\pi^{0}\eta^{\prime}$, $\eta\eta$, $\eta\eta^{\prime}$, and $\eta^{\prime}\eta^{\prime}$ at center-of-mass energies $2<Q<4\,\mathrm{GeV}$ in $k_{T}$ factorization, including the chirally enhanced twist-3 amplitudes and the two-gluon component of the $\eta^{(\prime)}$. The twist-3 amplitudes raise the hard cross sections by about an order of magnitude in all five channels. They bring $\eta\eta$ close to the Belle data, while $\pi^{0}\eta$ stays 3 to 5 times below and falls too slowly with energy. Varying the two-gluon distribution amplitude within its uncertainty changes the cross sections by about 2% in $\pi^{0}\eta$ and $\eta\eta$ but by up to 24% in the $\eta^{\prime}$ channels, making them its probe. The hard and handbag mechanisms each give nearly constant ratios $\sigma(\pi^{0}\eta)/\sigma(\pi^{0}\pi^{0})$ and $\sigma(\eta\eta)/\sigma(\pi^{0}\pi^{0})$, whereas below $3.2\,\mathrm{GeV}$ the measured $\pi^{0}\eta$ ratio lies above both predictions and the $\eta\eta$ ratio below them. Adding the handbag amplitude coherently, with its modulus fixed by the pion and kaon channels and its phase fitted, reproduces the $\pi^{0}\eta$ ratio up to $4\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the $\eta\eta$ ratio below $2.8\,\mathrm{GeV}$, and steepens $\sigma(\pi^{0}\eta)$ to a $Q^{-n}$ dependence with $n=9.7\pm1.6$, against the measured $10.5\pm1.2\pm0.5$. The energy dependence of the cross section ratios can thus be understood as the interference of two mechanisms of comparable size.

papers.title: Fortuitous Cancellation of Competing Effects in the Free Energy of Water Autoionization: Long-Range Electrostatics, System Size, and Nuclear Quantum Effects
papers.abstract: Few molecular processes are more fundamental to chemistry than the autoionization of water, whose equilibrium constant, $K_w \approx 10^{-14}$, underlies acid-base equilibria and the chemistry of life. Yet the molecular origins of the free energy cost of forming and separating ions remain incompletely understood. Efforts to explain it have been limited by the difficulty of modeling water reactivity in sufficient detail. Here we combine machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with spectral adaptive biasing force enhanced sampling to connect proton transfer and water wire configurations to the underlying free energy landscape. We identify competing influences of long-range electrostatics, system size, temperature, and nuclear quantum motion on the predicted ionization thermodynamics. The free energy surface extends from neutral water to ions separated beyond the solvent-separated ion pair (SSIP). It reveals a transition state in which a proton is shared between the second and third molecules of a three-membered water wire. The contact ion pair is unstable and the SSIP only weakly metastable, so determining pK$_w$ requires sampling longer wires. Long-range electrostatics raise the free energy at ion separations beyond $3\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. Models with comparable force errors give substantially different free energy profiles in this region. Increasing system size lowers the calculated pK$_w$, while nuclear quantum effects bring it closer to experiment and reproduce the higher pK$_w$ of D$_2$O relative to H$_2$O. These results establish a baseline for interpreting thermodynamic results from MLIP simulations in which charged and polar groups react and diffuse in finite cells. Our analysis also explains how cancellation among competing effects can yield ionization constants close to experiment even when simulations omit several physical contributions.

papers.title: Rotational Doppler Effect and Helimagnon Frequency Comb in Sliding Magnetic Spirals
papers.abstract: Collective spin motion can reshape magnon spectra by providing a dynamical magnetic background. Magnetic spirals offer a particularly clean setting, as they simultaneously host propagating helimagnons and a gapless Goldstone mode, i.e., the sliding of the spiral. Here, we show that once a helimagnon is excited and the spiral slides, the motion, which rotates the local spin frame, produces a thresholdless rotational Doppler shift of the helimagnon spectrum, with even winding for the linear mode and odd winding for its second harmonic. Stronger excitation generates one finite-momentum phason. Mixing of that phason with the helimagnon produces a helimagnon frequency comb only inside a finite driving window, spaced by the phason frequency fixed by the spiral length rather than by the sliding rate. These two scales are separable in a microwave experiment: the Doppler offset tracks the sliding velocity, whereas the comb spacing scales inversely with the length of the spiral.

papers.title: Magnetic-Field-Tuned Critical End Point and High-Field Phases in HoMn6Sn6
papers.abstract: Topological Kagome RMn6Sn6 materials, where R is a rare-earth, exhibit a rich variety of magnetic phases which provide an opportunity to understand how different spin textures affect topological and transport properties through the application of magnetic field H. In this work, we report experiments on single-crystal HoMn6Sn6, made possible by pulsed magnetic fields of up to 60 T, that permit high-field features of the field-temperature phase diagram to be studied in detail using magnetometry. Complementary, sensitive transport experiments over the same field range employ focused-ion-beam fabrication of novel strain-relieved HoMn6Sn6 devices. In agreement with meanfield calculations, we find a metamagnetic transition at 45 T with H||c between canted phases that ends in a critical end point at about 90 K. As far as we are aware, this is the only critical endpoint that is observed within the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals, and its temperature and field far exceed those of analogous phenomena in other materials. In the low-temperature metamagnetic region, HoMn6Sn6 shows large magnetoresistance, reaching 900 % at 60 T, in concert with Shubnikov de Haas oscillations that suggest a slight Fermi-surface contraction as the metamagnetic transition is crossed. A phase analysis of the oscillations suggests non-trivial band topology, although a firmer attribution must await detailed bandstructure calculations. Near the critical end point, we find deviations from Fermi-liquid behavior in the temperature-dependent magnetoresistance. In the metamagnetic region, the anomalous Hall contribution is not proportional to magnetization, and peaks at about 40 K, suggesting the role of enhanced spin fluctuations near the critical point. At higher temperatures, the anomalous Hall effect reappears at low fields, showing that the magnetization provided by the Ho and Mn sublattices independently affect the conductivity.

papers.title: Jaeger conjecture and Jaeger-Zhang conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that every signed planar graph $\widehat G$ of negative girth at least $\ell\geq 3$ satisfies $\chi_c(\widehat G)<\frac{2\ell}{\ell-2}$. As a consequence, for every integer $k\geq 1$, every planar graph $G$ of odd girth at least $4k+3$ satisfies $\chi_c(G)<\frac{2k+1}{k}$ and hence admits a homomorphism to $C_{2k+1}$. Our proofs build on recent results of Jafari on circular flows. In particular, Jafari proved that every $(4k+2)$-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly less than $2+\frac{1}{k}$. We revisit his theorem, providing an alternative proof that emphasizes the underlying graph-theoretic ideas. We also extend the result to signed graphs and weaken the connectivity assumption by imposing a lower bound only on the size of negative cuts. The key step is a small-correction lemma associated with a distribution on spanning trees. A splitting argument first gives the required correction in an even-degree graph; doubling the edges removes the degree-parity assumption. Plane duality then gives the coloring theorem. We discuss tightness of bounds in the end.

papers.title: Instant Payments After a Betting Ban: Evidence from Brazil
papers.abstract: Brazil has been facing major problems with delinquency, household debt, high interest rates, consumption, and access to credit. Betting has emerged in public debate as a possible contributing factor. On September 25, 2026, the federal government banned betting nationwide. We investigate how the ban affected instant payments (Pix). Our main finding, under the linear-trend specification, is that cumulative transaction counts over 37 days were approximately 8.37% below forecast, while settlement values were 10.83% lower. Both deviations were statistically significant under this specification.

papers.title: Competitive Balance Beyond Standings: Bayesian Inference for Latent Tiers and Structural Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Competitive balance has long been a central concern in sports economics, tied to outcome uncertainty, fan engagement, and the way leagues design their policies. Most existing measures of competitive balance are built from standings or winning percentages, which say little about how overall parity relates to the way teams sort into latent competitive tiers. We propose a Bayesian framework based on the Bradley-Terry model that jointly estimates the number of competitive tiers and team memberships. To capture the overall degree of competitive heterogeneity, we introduce a structural balance parameter defined on the unit interval within a hierarchical model, and we establish theoretical results giving this parameter a clear interpretation:it is directly tied to the separation between tiers, and overall heterogeneity depends on both the size and frequency of cross-tier differences. Importantly, structural balance is distinct from the information content of the schedule itself, so leagues with different numbers of teams and games can be compared on equal footing. Inference is carried out with an efficient posterior sampling algorithm that jointly handles team abilities, tier structure, home advantage, and structural balance. Simulation studies validate the proposed method, showing accurate recovery of the latent competitive structure and correct performance of the structural-balance testing procedure. Applied to the NBA and NFL, it reveals that the two leagues exhibit similar global structural balance despite very different competitive organizations: the NBA has three latent tiers, while the NFL has two broader ones, and the NFL's sparser schedule produces considerably more posterior uncertainty. Overall parity, it turns out, can mask quite different forms of competitive stratification-something standings-based measures alone cannot detect.

papers.title: Synchronized Optimal Transport Reconstructs Coupled Transcriptomic and Chromatin Dynamics
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA and ATAC data collected across developmental stages provide time-course snapshots of transcriptional and regulatory states. Since sequencing is destructive, trajectories between these snapshots must be inferred from independently sampled cell populations. Existing approaches typically infer continuous dynamics in a single modality or integrate RNA and ATAC in a shared representation. Here we present Cross-Omics Aligned Trajectory Inference (COATI), which extends unbalanced synchronized dynamical optimal transport to time-dependent cross-modal maps for reconstructing coupled trajectories in distinct RNA and ATAC state spaces. We evaluated COATI on synthetic benchmarks and four developmental datasets using held-out-stage reconstruction and lineage analyses. COATI improved reconstruction of cell populations at held-out stages, including recovery of chromatin-state heterogeneity within cell types, and better preserved developmental lineage relationships. The unbalanced formulation allows the inference of population mass changes, which were shown to associate with DNA-replication programs at early stages and lineage-maturation programs later in development. The coupled trajectories enabled analysis of lineage-specific transcriptional and chromatin changes and their temporal relationships during development. Lineage responses inferred by COATI agreed with independent CRISPR perturbation results, and the inferred regulatory patterns were consistent with independent epigenetic data.

papers.title: Plus Constructions and Canonical Induction for Green Categories
papers.abstract: We develop canonical induction for Green categories associated with Mackey systems. We establish a change-of-rings framework in which the lower-plus and upper-plus constructions are realized by induction and coinduction of modules. The two plus adjunctions yield the mark morphism, and, when the relevant group orders are invertible in the coefficient ring, Möbius inversion gives an explicit inverse. Using the resulting linearization and tom Dieck maps, we construct a canonical induction map, give an explicit formula for it, and characterize when it is a right inverse of linearization. In the classical setting of Mackey functors, our construction and splitting criterion recover Boltje's results.

papers.title: Conformationally frustrated epitaxy at heteromolecular interface
papers.abstract: Precise control of molecular heteroepitaxy offers a route to multilayer architectures with well-defined interfaces. However, the role of intramolecular flexibility in epitaxial matching remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the heteroepitaxy of intact 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene (BTB) on a molecular $\delta$-layer composed of fully deprotonated BTB molecules on Ag(111). Combining scanning tunneling microscopy, low-energy electron microscopy and diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and density functional theory, we identify the key interactions controlling molecular packing and epitaxial growth. We show that intermolecular bonding motifs are preserved on the molecular template, but their lattice parameters and molecular conformations change as compared to a silver surface. Individual molecules exhibit distinct appearances in scanning tunneling microscopy, consistent with site-dependent conformational variations identified by theory. Our calculations reveal that the competition between molecule-substrate interactions and conformational energy produces different compromise geometries, resulting in conformational frustration at the epitaxial interface. Crucially, constraining BTB into a planar geometry changes the preferred lateral adsorption positions, demonstrating that molecular flexibility directly modifies the energetic preferences for epitaxial registry. Comparison with more rigid molecular overlayers further supports this interpretation. Our findings reveal that molecular flexibility contributes to epitaxial matching by allowing unfavorable molecule-substrate interactions to be compensated by energetically favorable conformations while preserving the intermolecular network.

papers.title: Self-injection-locked dark-soliton Kerr optical frequency combs with high even-order normal dispersion
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate dissipative dark-soliton (DDS) microcombs under the action of pure high even-order normal (HEON) dispersion in a microresonator with the self-injection locking (SIL). Pure 4th, 6th, 10th, and 14th-order normal dispersion can support DDSs formed by interlocked switching waves, directly excited through a SIL-based turnkey scheme without detuning sweeps. Compared to the pure 4th-order case, the switching-wave tail oscillation period increases and its decay rate decreases with the increase of the dispersion order. Although the overall comb bandwidth narrows, the number of non-pump comb lines above a common absolute power threshold increases. Furthermore, the feedback phase controls the DDS duty cycle and intracavity comb-line power distribution, while the increase of the pump power improves the estimated pump-to-comb output conversion efficiency.

papers.title: Unlocking Pandora's Secrets: Probing the Thermodynamics of Abell 2744
papers.abstract: Abell 2744 (Pandora's Cluster) is a massive galaxy cluster undergoing multiple mergers, characterized by a highly disturbed X-ray morphology, elevated intracluster medium (ICM) temperatures, and several radio relics associated with merger driven shocks. We present NuSTAR observations of Abell 2744 aimed at mapping its thermodynamic structure and constraining the presence of inverse Compton (IC) scattering from relativistic electrons. We measure the temperature distribution across the cluster and identify a prominent shock front with a Mach number of $\mathcal{M} = 1.58^{+0.42}_{-0.30}$, aligning with the southeastern boundary of the radio halo. The global NuSTAR spectra are modeled with single- and two-temperature thermal components, as well as thermal plus power-law models to test for IC emission. The spectra are well described by purely thermal models with an average temperature of $kT \approx 11$ keV, and we find no significant evidence for non-thermal hard X-ray emission. We derive a 90\% confidence upper limit on the $20-80$ keV IC flux of $ F_{\rm nt} < 2.31 \times 10^{-12} erg~s^{-1}~cm^{-2}$. Combining this with 1.5 GHz diffuse radio measurements from the VLA, we estimate a lower limit on the average magnetic field strength of $B > 0.2 \ \rm{\mu G}$.

papers.title: From spectroscopy to quantum dynamics: assessing reduced models of a NaCs molecular gate
Bayesian Unit-level Quantile Modeling with Application to Wealth Data
papers.abstract: Modeling wealth quantiles over time and space and across fine-grained demographic classifications is of vital importance to policy makers. However, such data present unique challenges for standard small area estimation methodologies because they are highly skewed and heavy-tailed with both positive and negative values. Traditional area-level modeling and design-based approaches struggle to capture these features. Meanwhile, existing unit-level methodology frequently treats the survey design as ignorable and does not apply to surveys that are repeated over time. Often the analysis is restricted to alternative response variables that are non-negative, such as poverty indicators or income. To overcome these limitations, we propose a Bayesian, asymmetric Laplace pseudolikelihood model that is able to capture the major features of wealth while adjusting for survey weights and accounting for both spatial and temporal dependence. We present a Gibbs sampling algorithm for our model, as well as a variational Bayes algorithm for fast computation. We apply the method to the Survey of Income and Program Participation to characterize geographic, temporal, and demographic variation in the distribution of U.S. household wealth, including for sparsely sampled domains where direct estimates are unavailable or unstable.

papers.title: Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
Containment Problems in Convex Sets
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $C$ be a compact, convex subset of the plane that contains the origin in its interior. We study the problem of finding two points $p$ and $q$ of $P$ with the property that any homothet of $C$ that contains $p$ and $q$ must contain at least a constant fraction of the points of $P$. We give proofs for several cases. When $C$ is strictly convex we achieve a fraction of $1/5$, and when $C$ is a general convex region we achieve a fraction of $1/6e$. We show how the ideas of this second bound can be used to prove a lower bound for a version of the problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $C$ is a $d$-ball. We also consider a few special cases. When $C$ is a triangle we get a lower bound of $1/12$, and when we allow that triangle to be rotated by $\pi$ radians in addition to being scaled and translated we get a lower bound of $1/768$. In proving this last result, we improve the state of the art on the version of this problem in three dimensions, where $C$ is a parallelepiped. We also consider the algorithmic aspects of finding such a pair of points.

papers.title: Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology
papers.abstract: In the lower-star filtration (LSF), simplices are assigned filtration values according to the maximum-vertex rule, with each simplex entering the filtration when its highest-valued vertex appears. A limitation of this construction is that some higher-dimensional simplices may enter simultaneously with their boundary faces, causing certain topological features to be filled immediately upon formation and thus not appear in the resulting persistence diagram. To address this limitation, we propose three alternative filtration methods: the \(\varepsilon\)-lower-star filtration (ELSF), the \(L_p\) filtration (LpF), and the softmax filtration (SMF). {ELSF introduces a dimension-dependent delay to the maximum-vertex rule,} allowing higher-dimensional simplices to enter the filtration after their boundary faces, whereas {LpF and SMF use aggregation functions that depend on all vertex values rather} than solely on their maximum. By modifying how filtration values are assigned, these methods allow simplices to enter the filtration more progressively, so that topological features such as loops and voids may persist over longer filtration intervals rather than being filled immediately. Consequently, the resulting persistence diagrams may include persistence features that are not observed under LSF, potentially providing useful information for distinguishing data populations. Experimental results on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed filtration methods are computationally efficient and can provide greater sensitivity to structural differences in the data than LSF.

papers.title: Kinetic Cluster Embedding for Qubit Decoherence in Dissipative Spin Baths
An improved isodiametric inequality for convex surfaces
papers.abstract: Alexandrov conjectured that every closed convex surface of area $A$ and intrinsic diameter $D$ satisfies $A/D^2\leq\pi/2$. Using an averaging argument over the curvature measure, we prove that every closed convex surface satisfies $A/D^2\leq2\pi/3$, improving the best previously known bound.

papers.title: KCWI Observations of Type 2 Quasar-driven Ionized Outflows at z~0.1
papers.abstract: AGN-driven outflows play a crucial role in regulating star formation in galaxies. These outflows are known to be multi-phase, and the characterization of the kinematics, extent, and energetics of each gas phase is needed to obtain a full picture of the outflow properties and impact. This study presents Keck Cosmic Web Imager (KCWI) integral field spectroscopy of the ionized gas outflow properties in seven low redshift (z<0.1) quasars---six Type 2 AGN and one narrow-line Type 1 AGN---providing insight into the warm ionized outflows in these luminous AGN. With the large field-of-view and high sensitivity of KCWI, these data reveal both larger ionized outflow extents than were previously known for these sources and uncover the existence of additional high-velocity kinematic components in the ionized outflows of these luminous AGN. We find (a) a high incidence (50-70%) of multiple outflows on scales of 4--10 kpc and (b) trends between the outflow extent, kinematics, and the ionized mass and energy outflow rates. These trends imply that the faster and often smaller outflows carry higher mass and energy outflow rates than the slower, larger outflows. We also find that the ionized gas outflows reach as far as the known extent of narrow-line ionized gas emission in AGN, which is known to depend weakly on AGN luminosity. This work highlights the utility of the current generation of wide-field integral field spectrographs on 8--10m class telescopes for studying quasar-driven outflows.

papers.title: Differentiation of tepui groupoids and the holonomy groupoid of singular foliations
papers.abstract: Tepui groupoids are a generalization of Lie groupoids which allow the arrow space to be singular, as is the case for holonomy groupoids of singular foliations. We construct a Lie differentiation functor for a large class of tepui groupoids. When restricted to effective and source-connected tepui groupoids, this differentiation recovers the correspondence between holonomy groupoids and their underlying singular foliations.

papers.title: Interferometric survey of stellar parameters. Reliable methodology for a direct measurement of the angular diameter in exoplanet host stars
authors: (2) The CHARA Array of Georgia State University
papers.abstract: Since their pioneer observations more than thirty years ago, exoplanets have been a major topic among the astrophysics community. Despite their ubiquity, our knowledge of planetary parameters and internal compositions still mostly relies on stellar quantities estimated through evolutionary models, which suffer from a calibration bias, preventing the community to have accurate discussions on the diversity of planets across the Universe. We use our sample to demonstrate the current best reachable precision of the CHARA Array to be $\sim$ 2% on radius determination, with an error budget dominated by the uncertainty on the angular diameter, while systematics are shown to be of the order of 1% thanks to our methodology. While the precision matches values found in the literature, we demonstrate the uniqueness of the present study in the relevance of the results put forward. Finally, we show that our methods naturally translate into an improved accuracy of the planetary parameters, along with an improvement in precision by $\sim$ 50% in radius and $\sim$ 30% in mass.

papers.title: Growth and fabrication of advanced PbTe-Pb quantum devices
papers.abstract: We report recent progress in the growth and fabrication of advanced PbTe-Pb Majorana devices for three-terminal correlation experiments. A critical prerequisite for these devices is a continuous Pb film spanning from the PbTe nanowire to the substrate. In previous studies, PbTe nanowires were spatially separated from the substrate mask, making them unable to fulfill this requirement. To address this issue, we have developed a new growth and fabrication approach. Key fabrication steps are introduced between the PbTe growth and Pb deposition. The top facet of the PbTe nanowire is covered with a Te capping layer before breaking the ultra-high vacuum, enabling ex situ processing for subsequent steps. The mask is then removed, followed by the fabrication of shadow walls. After reloading the chip into the growth chamber, the Te protection layer is removed through thermal decomposition, and the Pb film is subsequently deposited. Notably, a pristine PbTe-Pb interface with an in-situ-equivalent quality can be achieved despite the ex-situ processing. Our technique facilitates the develop of advanced PbTe-Pb quantum devices with complex designs, paving the way toward the realization of topological qubits.

papers.title: Neutral-atom quantum features as complementary structural encodings for graph learning
Reflexive polytopes can have doubly exponentially many vertices
papers.abstract: Reflexive polytopes are lattice polytopes containing the origin in their interior such that also the dual polytope is a lattice polytope. On the basis of low-dimensional observations and of bounds known for special classes of reflexive polytopes, the second author conjectured in 2004 that the number of vertices of $d$-dimensional reflexive polytopes is bounded from above by $6^{d/2}$. In this note, we present counterexamples showing that this conjecture is false in every dimension $d \ge 8$. In fact, rather surprisingly, in sufficiently large dimensions $d$ the number of vertices (equivalently, by duality, the number of facets) can be as large as theoretically possible, namely doubly exponential in $d$. These results were found using GPT-6.1 Sol.

papers.title: Multilevel kernel approximation of log-Euclidean manifold-valued functions
papers.abstract: We study kernel approximation and multilevel residual correction for functions with values in a manifold that admits a global logarithm onto a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, such as positive definite matrices, exponential Lie groups, and Hadamard manifolds. Approximating in logarithmic coordinates keeps the approximant on the manifold and transfers Hilbert-space error estimates verbatim. To express these errors in the natural geometry of the target, we prove metric comparisons. In particular, we obtain a sharp, scale-invariant bound between the log-Euclidean and affine-invariant distances on positive definite matrices, with a constant that depends only on condition numbers. For multilevel approximation, compactly supported kernels scaled to the fill distance give algebraic convergence with sparse, uniformly well-conditioned systems. These guarantees require appropriate sample locations and approximation scales. Compact groups are treated through a principal logarithm, where a bi-invariant metric gives error bounds with constant one. Finally, the log-Euclidean and Karcher means differ by $\mathcal O(r^3)$ near the identity and by $\mathcal O(r^2)$ around a general point, where $r$ is the logarithmic data radius and the second bound is sharp.

papers.title: Burgess' bounds with prime moduli
papers.abstract: Let $S_{\chi}(N)= \sum_{n\leq N} \chi(n)$, where $\chi$ is a Dirichlet character modulo a prime $p$. For integral $r\geq 2$, Burgess gave bounds of the shape $S_{\chi}(N) \ll N^{1-1/r} p^{(r+1)/(4r^{2})} \log p$. The factor of $\log p$ was reduced by several authors. We show that it can be removed completely.

papers.title: Left-Invariant Kernels of the Hodge-de Rham Operator on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We determine the kernel of the Hodge--de Rham operator on left-invariant differential forms for the seven customary families of three-dimensional Lorentzian metric Lie algebras. Every parameter stratum is treated, including zero structure constants, singular bracket matrices, and null modular directions. If $\theta(X)=\mathrm{tr}\,\mathrm{ad}_X$ is the modular character, the full kernel is the direct sum of constants, the space $K=\mathrm{Ann}([\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{g}])\cap\theta^\perp$, its Hodge dual, and the volume forms. We give explicit real bases in all seven families and compute the exterior differential and geometric codifferential on every basis form. The non-unimodular calculation remains valid without the customary extra normalization conditions, and hence also covers metric representatives omitted by those conditions. The resulting dimensions are $2,4,6$, or $8$; the two middle-degree dimensions agree. Explicit examples distinguish the kernel of the first-order operator from the kernel of its square. All assertions concern smooth left-invariant forms, with no square-integrability condition.

papers.title: Galois lines for the maximal curve with the second largest genus in characteristic two
papers.abstract: We determine all Galois lines for the embedding of the maximal curve with the second largest genus in characteristic two into $\mathbb{P}^{3}$ induced by its Frobenius linear series. We also determine the associated Galois groups.

papers.title: Sensing-Based Communication: A Non-Orthogonal Passive Reflection Framework for ISAC
papers.abstract: While integrating uplink without disrupting the primary downlink remains a critical challenge for existing reflective communication systems, this paper proposes a non-orthogonal passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism termed Sensing-based Communication. Originating from and validated within an optical retro-reflective system, this mechanism possesses an underlying wave-agnostic architecture with the potential to be generalized across other physical modalities. It leverages incident downlink signals for parasitic modulation via passive tags. By relying solely on fundamental on-off keying (OOK) reflection, the tag unifies the reflective sensing channel and the uplink communication channel, and simultaneously achieves both sensing and duplex communication. Consequently, our approach introduces uplink capability without sacrificing the downlink data rate or consuming additional spectrum resources. At the receiver, we design a joint decoding architecture combining cross-correlation computation and successive interference cancelation (SIC) to fully exploit the degrees of freedom in broadband signals for multi-user interference suppression. We derive closed-form expressions for the interference and bit error rate (BER) assuming zero-mean Gaussian signals. Using an experimental testbed, we validate the pivotal theoretical finding, the scaling relationship of SINR with signal bandwidth and cross-correlation time--where linear regression yields a strong goodness-of-fit with $R^2 = 0.9688$. Furthermore, evaluations under noise-like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms exhibit high consistency between theoretical derivations and simulation data ($R^2 = 0.9372$, mean absolute percentage error, $\text{MAPE} = 14\%$), confirming the model's accuracy and waveform generalizability.

papers.title: Electrohydrodynamic interactions of two Quincke rotors: asymptotic theory and boundary element simulations
papers.abstract: Weakly conducting spheres suspended in a leaky dielectric fluid can undergo spontaneous Quincke rotation when the applied electric field exceeds a critical value. We investigate how electric and hydrodynamic interactions modify this instability and the subsequent rotation of two spheres at fixed separation and orientation. Starting from electric dipole and hydrodynamic rotlet interactions, we develop a systematic far-field asymptotic theory. Away from onset, slow drift of the rotation axes makes a regular expansion fail at long times. A multiple-scale expansion gives slow phase equations that select the axes according to pair orientation and field strength. Near onset, weak interactions produce corrections comparable to the isolated rotation magnitude. A detuned multiple-scale expansion gives coupled equations for the transverse dipole amplitudes. Their linearization identifies four collective rotation modes, whose critical fields and steady branches with one active mode are determined together with their stability. At leading order near onset, electric interaction shifts all four modal thresholds equally, whereas hydrodynamic interaction makes counter-rotation appear first for pair angles below $\cos^{-1}(1/\sqrt3)\simeq54.7^\circ$ and co-rotation above it. Away from onset, the angle separating stable counter-rotation from stable co-rotation increases with field strength. Boundary element method (BEM) simulations place onset within a field interval for each configuration and resolve the growth and relaxation of rotation. Steady-speed comparisons show how pair orientation changes the balance between electric and hydrodynamic effects. We compare the unexpanded dipole-rotlet model of Das and Saintillan [Phys. Rev. E 87, 043014 (2013)] with our asymptotic theory and BEM simulations.

papers.title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.abstract: We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $\mu$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-Élie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.

papers.title: Proof of the Cordero-Torregrosa Conjecture and an Improved Order Bound for Paired Jacobian Evaluations
papers.abstract: In solving systems of nonlinear equations, one of the main objectives is to construct iterative methods that attain high orders of convergence using as few evaluations as possible. However, the information a method obtains during each iteration imposes limitations on the order it can guarantee. The Cordero--Torregrosa conjecture proposes a bound on this order in terms of the number of evaluations of the function and its Jacobian. In this work, we prove this bound for the universal local order of one iteration, without requiring the number of Jacobian evaluations to be less than or equal to the number of function evaluations. In particular, our result also covers the case in which more evaluations of the Jacobian than of the function are performed. The proof encompasses deterministic, causal, memoryless methods whose rules may be arbitrary, without imposing rationality, continuity, or computability conditions. Moreover, we prove that when each Jacobian evaluation is performed at a point where the value of the function is already known, a more restrictive bound on the order of convergence can be obtained. Finally, we propose a new conjecture that establishes a refined bound through a product of factors determined by the distribution of evaluations, under additional dimensional conditions. These results provide a better understanding of the limitations imposed by the available information and raise new possibilities for studying high-order iterative methods.

papers.title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
papers.abstract: Reward models used for off-policy evaluation (OPE) are commonly selected using held-out data. When sample size and context dimension grow proportionally, the difference in test risk between models fitted on the full sample and on a fixed fraction of it need not vanish. Held-out evaluation can therefore consistently estimate the test risk of the model trained on the smaller sample, but because the relative ranking of candidate reward models can change after full-data refitting, held-out selection can be suboptimal. We develop an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk under the target policy using only its training observations. This enables early stopping along the full-data gradient-descent trajectory without sample splitting. For neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, context-dependent multi-index target policies, and known context-independent logging, we prove uniform consistency of our criterion over a fixed finite set of gradient-descent iterates and a near-oracle guarantee for the selected reward model. The same correction yields a doubly robust estimator that consistently estimates the true policy value without sample splitting, even when reward-model prediction error does not vanish. Experiments show decreasing risk-estimation error as dimension grows at a fixed sample-to-dimension ratio, and improved reward-model selection relative to held-out baselines. Empirically, our correction also reduces the root mean squared error of doubly robust value estimates computed from the same data used to fit and select the reward models.

papers.title: Exact optimality of augmented order-of-addition designs
papers.abstract: We prove that, for the pairwise-ordering model with at least three components, adding any run to an order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design among all exact designs of the enlarged size, allowing replication. We also establish the corresponding result for foldover designs: adding any reversal pair to a foldover order-of-addition orthogonal array gives a $D$-optimal design within the foldover class at the enlarged size. Both augmentations also minimise the average prediction variance and a covariance-scaled information discrepancy, and maximise the minimum relative efficiency. The key step represents the scaled discrepancy through signed comparisons of triples and derives a sharp integer lower bound; classical spectral inequalities then give the exact-size optima, and signed four-component relative-order counts characterise equality. Complete reversal pairs additionally protect the estimation of pairwise-ordering effects against arbitrary reversal-invariant nuisance means. At the smallest estimable five-component foldover size, exact enumeration identifies five determinant-optimal classes with different prediction and balance properties, and a seven-component example shows that deleting a reversal pair need not be optimal even when it minimises the discrepancy. Constructions through ten components illustrate the attained run sizes.

papers.title: Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.

papers.title: Blind Noise Equalization for Large Data Matrices under General Variance Profiles
papers.abstract: Low-rank approximation is a basic tool for inference from large and noisy data matrices. However, when noise variances differ across entries, a setting known as heteroskedasticity, the noise can distort the observed spectrum, producing spurious components and obscuring weak signals. To address these challenges, we develop BRINE (Blind Resolvent-based Iterative Noise Equalizer), a data-driven procedure that iteratively rescales rows and columns to equalize the average noise variance across both dimensions. Under suitable conditions, this procedure restores the Marchenko-Pastur law for the noise spectrum and can amplify signal components without prior knowledge of the signal or noise structure. A key idea underlying our approach is to equalize the diagonal entries of the data resolvent as a proxy for equalizing the unknown noise variances. At the population level, we identify a potential function that characterizes this equalization and motivates an iterative minimization procedure. We prove convergence of the iterations to the true equalizer for arbitrary positive variance profiles, with a geometric rate under mild conditions. The updates can be estimated directly from noisy data, and we establish probabilistic error bounds for the scaling factors. Simulations and experiments across diverse biological data modalities and preprocessing pipelines illustrate the effectiveness of our approach.

papers.title: Multi-Model Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Transceiver Beamforming and Device Grouping
papers.abstract: This paper considers uplink communication design for training multiple independent machine learning models via wireless federated learning. To reduce communication delay, we utilize multi-antenna beamforming and propose a multi-model over-the-air (M-OTA) uplink transmission and aggregation method for simultaneous training of multiple models. Devices are formed into groups for local model training based on the model assignments per communication round and simultaneously perform OTA aggregation over a multi-access channel. Based on the M-OTA transmission and reception process, we formulate a joint optimization of transmit and receive beamforming and device grouping over $T$ communication rounds to maximize the training convergence rates of all models. We analyze the per-model optimality gap, which captures the impact of noisy aggregation and inter-model interference on the learning performance. We further show that the $T$-round joint optimization problem can be decomposed into per-round online optimization to devise solutions. Following this, we propose a device grouping strategy that explores channel correlation among devices to maximize OTA aggregation performance. Furthermore, we present a low-complexity iterative algorithm for joint transmit-receive beamforming with closed-form updates. Simulation shows that our proposed M-OTA approach substantially outperforms the conventional single-model sequential OTA approach and other commonly used beamforming schemes.

papers.title: Features of Non-Local Quantum Correlations in Nuclei
papers.abstract: Classical simulation of quantum many-body systems is challenged by the combined effects of entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic). Non-local magic, $M^{\mathrm{NL}}_\alpha$, quantifies the component of non-stabilizerness that cannot be removed by local unitary transformations and provides a measure of quantum complexity beyond entanglement alone. It is bounded from below by the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum, ${F}_A$. We calculate stabilizer Rényi entropies, non-local magic, entanglement-spectrum antiflatness, and entanglement entropy in shell-model ground states of more than 260 even-even, odd-even, and odd-odd nuclei, using a bipartition into proton and neutron sectors. We find that the previously established bound $4{F}_A\leq{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}}$ holds for every nucleus studied and approaches saturation in the limit of separable states. Odd-odd nuclei exhibit markedly different patterns of entanglement and magic compared with even-even and odd-even systems, revealing distinctive signatures of proton-neutron quantum correlations and providing new insight into the complexity generated by nuclear interactions.

papers.title: On Lipschitz Explosion in Deep Neural Networks with Normalization: Consequences for Optimization and Adversarial Robustness
papers.abstract: Can a network look stable at every layer and still be exponentially unstable as a whole? The Lipschitz constant of a neural network is a basic stability quantity appearing in optimization guarantees, generalization bounds, and robustness certificates.
