As AI systems take on a growing role in synthesising scientific evidence, these findings highlight the need to evaluate how they use evidence to reach causal conclusions, alongside whether their interventions succeed.

papers.title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
Descending Everest, Part II: Oracle Complexity of Minimizing a Sum of Convex $(L_0,L_1)$-Smooth Functions
papers.abstract: We study the minimization of the average of $n$ convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth functions: the Hessian norm of each function is bounded by an affine function of its gradient norm. We assume known upper bounds $R$ on the distance from the starting point to a minimizer and $\delta$ on the difference between the minimum of the average and the average of the infima of the components. We derive upper and lower bounds on the oracle complexity of reaching accuracy $\varepsilon$ in function value in expectation. Up to logarithmic factors, both bounds are of order $n(1+(L_1R)^{2/3}) +\sqrt{\frac{n(L_0+L_1^2\delta)R^2}{\varepsilon}+n(L_1R)^2}$. The upper bound is attained by the proposed method YETI. The method combines ideas of accelerated proximal methods and variance reduction methods with a heuristic for choosing additional points. The number of oracle calls made by the heuristic is bounded, which preserves the upper bound on the total number of queries needed to reach the target accuracy. In the experiments, YETI is compared with first-order methods on synthetic problems and Poisson regression problems. We also examine the stopping criterion and the effect of the heuristic separately. The lower bound is obtained by an explicit construction of families of instances that are hard for any first-order method.

papers.title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum. We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_\sigma\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.

papers.title: Multiple windows of eigenstate-selective delocalization in a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice
papers.abstract: We investigate localization in a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice with a real quasiperiodic onsite potential of strength $W$ and a staggered imaginary quasiperiodic modulation of strength $\lambda$. Using the inverse participation ratio (IPR), normalized participation ratio (NPR), fractal dimension $D_2$, transfer-matrix Lyapunov exponent, and wave-packet dynamics, we find a strongly non-monotonic and state-dependent response. At fixed $\lambda$, varying $W$ yields two distinct delocalization windows, whereas varying $\lambda$ at fixed $W$ produces a single re-entrant delocalization window. These regimes arise within selected eigenstate sectors, where localized states coexist with extended or critical states, leading to mobility-edge-like behavior. The corresponding suppression of the Lyapunov exponent and enhancement of the dynamical RMS spreading are consistent with the IPR, NPR, and $D_2$ results. Finite-size scaling confirms the persistence of the re-entrant features, while the complex-energy spectrum resolves their state-selective structure. The resulting phase boundaries delineate distinct localization regimes in the $(W,\lambda)$ plane. Our results show that the interplay between quasiperiodicity and a staggered non-Hermitian modulation sharing the same quasiperiodic spatial structure can generate re-entrant, state-dependent localization, with implications for localization and dynamics in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattices.

papers.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

papers.title: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Experimental Reasoning
papers.abstract: An experimental agent can succeed for the wrong reasons. Evaluations, however, often focus on the outcome, not the experiments, evidence, and inferences that produced it. We introduce LUCA, a configurable synthetic world for evaluating this process under fully known ground truth. Agents learn unknown regulatory systems through budgeted experimentation, then predict unseen interventions, diagnose hidden faults, and attempt rescues. This setup allows us to evaluate experiment selection, prediction, diagnosis, and intervention separately. Across seven frontier LLMs and three baselines, these capabilities dissociate sharply. Agents frequently rescue malfunctioning systems while diagnosing the wrong fault; diagnosis varies 7x across models while prediction varies only 1.4x. Models also adopt surprisingly different experimental strategies, and greater exploration does not reliably yield better performance. In one failure mode, agents often perform the experiment needed to distinguish competing causes, but still fail to use the resulting evidence. LUCA turns these hidden failures into measurable behaviours, providing a controlled environment to study where experimental agents succeed and fail. Code: this https URL .

papers.title: Classification Aggregation with Multiple Memberships
papers.abstract: People face the problem of classifying objects into categories while aggregating their opinions. We axiomatically study such a classification aggregation problem with multiple memberships, meaning that each individual assigns one category to every object, whereas the resulting classification may assign more than one category. Under the natural settings and axioms (i.e., Independence and Supportiveness), each of our new axioms -- Responsibility, Split Stability and Rejection Stability -- characterises what we call the junta rules. The rules assign a category to an object exactly when some member of a fixed coalition does so. The coalitions that can secure an assignment form a grill, a topological structure implied by an ultrafilter. Hence, the study parallels the literature on Arrow's theorem characterised by the decisive coalition structures. An infinite population setting is also investigated to clarify the differences among the axioms.

papers.title: Tracking the evolution of sub-Neptunes. II. The radius valley on gyrochronological ages
papers.abstract: The radius valley separating super-Earths from sub-Neptunes is understood as a signature of atmospheric mass loss, but the timescale over which it develops remains poorly constrained. We investigate the age evolution of the radius valley and the super-Earth population around FGK stars using gyrochronological ages. We select $746$ planets around $510$ FGK hosts with reliable gyrochronological ages between $0.1$ and $4$ Gyr. A subset of $581$ planets around $404$ hosts, for which detection and confirmation completeness can be characterised, forms the reference sample. We measure the valley morphology and its locus in the period-radius plane, and infer the intrinsic super-Earth fraction with a selection-conditioned mixture model that accounts for stellar-age uncertainties. The intrinsic super-Earth fraction increases primarily during the first $\sim2$ Gyr, with no significant subsequent evolution. An exponential approach-to-plateau model places $90\%$ of this increase within $1.9$ Gyr at $90\%$ credibility. The radius valley is consistently resolved from $\sim1.5$ Gyr onwards, with no significant evolution in its depth or width. Its minimum may shift from $\sim1.5\,R_\oplus$ before $\sim2$ Gyr to $\sim1.8\,R_\oplus$ at older ages, accompanied by a change in the shape of the super-Earth radius distribution, although these changes are only suggestive. This evolution is consistent with atmospheric loss continuing up to approximately $1$-$2$ Gyr for a fraction of planets. The tentative shift of the valley minimum towards larger radii may indicate that planets with more massive cores complete envelope loss later, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish between atmospheric-loss mechanisms.

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of the baryon octet and flavor dependence in an NJL quark--diquark model
papers.abstract: We calculate the gravitational form factors $A$, $J$ and $D$ of the baryon octet in a Nambu--Jona-Lasinio quark--diquark model with proper-time regularization. With the diquark poles used for the octet spectrum, the $\Sigma$ has the smallest $|D(0)|$ and the largest $r_D$, $0.675~\mathrm{fm}$ compared with $0.637~\mathrm{fm}$ for the nucleon. Its $A$ radius is smaller than the nucleon's. Along the strange-quark mass trajectory, $r_D^\Sigma-r_D^N$ is negative at the lowest nonzero mass and positive at the other three. The difference $r_A^\Sigma-r_A^N$ is negative at all four masses. At a common spatial resolution, the $\Sigma$ also has the weakest pressure and shear peaks.

papers.title: Perfect 1-factorisations of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group
papers.abstract: A perfect 1-factorisation (P1F) of $K_{2n}$ is a partition of its edges into $2n-1$ perfect matchings, any two of which form a Hamiltonian cycle. Exhaustive classification is known only up to $K_{16}$. We present a method for the exhaustive generation, up to isomorphism, of perfect 1-factorisations with a non-trivial automorphism group, which reduces the search tree far enough to make $K_{18}$ and beyond feasible. It combines two ideas. For automorphism groups of order greater than 2, classical results of Ihrig on the automorphisms of P1Fs are used as tools that reject almost all prescribed cycle types without search. For the order-2 case, which dominates, candidates are recalculated from inherited compatibility lists, in the spirit of Gill and Wanless, with an outer loop over two further rows that keeps those lists small, and Ihrig's results restrict the first factor. As the numerical proof of the method we compute all 10,710 P1Fs of $K_{18}$ with a non-trivial automorphism group; before, only six were known.

papers.title: Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. Our main contribution is the development of an easy-to-implement observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. Furthermore, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. Numerical simulations indicate the same optimisation problem can recover the true profile for the nonlinear versions of the same dispersive water-wave models.

papers.title: CuriousTogether: Implications of Curiosity and Cultural Grounding in Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent settings, exhibiting emergent collective behaviors, yet the role of curiosity as a driver of such dynamics remains understudied. We introduce CuriousTogether, a framework evaluating curiosity-driven multi-agent LLM interactions across three complementary dimensions: novelty-seeking, epistemic and social curiosity. Across eight tasks spanning reasoning, creative generation, and social bias mitigation, curiosity-guided multi-agent settings yield improvements over non-curious ones on seven out of eight tasks, with gains of up to 20.6% in story generation (semantic diversity) and a 14.9 pp reduction in stereotype rates. Furthermore, country-conditioned cultural grounding show benefits for story generation and social tasks, but can hurt precision-oriented reasoning. Finally, we show that inference-time multi-agent curiosity-based approach offers favorable quality-token trade-offs, compared with single-agent baselines. Together, these findings support curiosity-guided interaction as a practical mechanism for improving multi-agent collaboration, with downstream benefits for reasoning, creative, and societal tasks.

papers.title: Representability of Graphical Symplectic Matroids
papers.abstract: Chow associated with every finite multigraph $G$ a symplectic matroid $\GraphS{G}$ on the signed edge set $E\sqcup E^{*}$, whose restrictions to transversals are frame matroids of signed graphs, and Sarvepalli asked which of these matroids are representable. For a connected graph containing a cycle, we show that every isotropic representation of $S(G)$ admits an incidence-flow normal form. The remaining representation conditions are expressed through its admissible minors. Consequently, if $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable, then the bridgeless part of $G$ has a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow. In characteristic other than two, $\GraphS{G}$ is representable if and only if every non-loop edge on a cycle has a parallel mate. In characteristic two, we characterize the loopless graphs without two vertex-disjoint cycles by the existence of a nowhere-zero $(\F,+)$-flow, and we show that rigidly linked short cycles, and hence subdivisions of the prism, are obstructions. For $3$-connected simple graphs this gives a complete answer: $\GraphS{G}$ is $\F$-representable if and only if $\F$ has characteristic two, $G$ has no two vertex-disjoint cycles, and either $|\F|>2$ or $G\cong K_5$. In particular, the matroid of the Petersen graph is representable over no field. Finally, the admissible corank--nullity polynomial of an arbitrary symplectic matroid is intrinsic and satisfies a three-term contraction identity. For graphical symplectic matroids, this becomes a deletion-contraction recursion that closes up once marked vertices are allowed, and polynomials built from enveloping matroids agree with it exactly for sheltering envelopes.

papers.title: Sharp digirth bounds for C(k,k)-subdivisions in digraphs
papers.abstract: For an integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. We extend a problem of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud [European J. Combin. 122 (2024)] on subdivisions of $C(k,k)$ to digraphs with several vertices of out-degree one. Following the sharp result of Chen et al. [ arXiv:2610.38574v1 (2026)] for at most one such vertex, we determine the exact digirth threshold when at most $r\ge4$ such vertices are permitted. Specifically, for all integers $k\ge2$ and $r\ge4$, every digraph of minimum out-degree at least one, with at most $r$ vertices of out-degree one and digirth at least $r(k-1)+1$, contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$.

papers.title: A Spectral Renormalization-Group View of Learning
papers.abstract: We study how the layers in deep neural networks (NNs) converge, using Wilsonian Renormalization-Group (RG) ideas to organize the spectral picture. During training, these layers often develop heavy-tailed power-law (PL) spectra, and the strongest checkpoints often appear near the PL exponent $\alpha\approx 2$. This pattern raises a simple question: why should this value mark a well-trained layer? The answer is both statistical and physical. Our statistical hypothesis is that $\alpha=2$ marks the boundary between stable if not optimal learning and overfitting via non-self-averaging. The physical answer is that the same value makes the spectral energy gain scale evenly across logarithmic spectral scales, which is the proposed Wilsonian marginal condition. We then apply the ERG trace-log condition, the proposed SETOL theory, which we justify by taking volume-preserving, scale-invariant transformations to remove arbitrary layer scale along the proposed RG flow. The resulting spectral RG flow connects the HTSR and SETOL theories to optimizers such as Muon, and motivates a new optimizer extension, WW-PGD. Together, these results point toward a spectral Renormalization-Group view of learning, in which NNs may approach shared spectral structure in the settings studied here.

papers.title: Behavior Graphs: Unsupervised Graph Structures for Interpreting Robot Deployment Data
papers.abstract: Data flywheels promise continuous improvement via insights from deployment data. Understanding how the deployed model succeeds and fails can steer subsequent data collection towards patching failures and reinforcing successes. However, robot deployments create large volumes of high-dimensional rollout data, which is challenging to understand and confidently ground data collection decisions in. To make deployment data easier to analyze and act on, we propose behavior graphs, which compress policy rollouts into a single interpretable, directed graph. We construct the graphs by learning to identify similar behavior modes across rollouts, connecting the behaviors temporally, and finally linking them to outcomes. In a user study on three real-world tasks, where participants analyzed rollouts to choose a data collection strategy, 16 of 18 preferred behavior graphs to rollout videos, reaching comparable conclusions with 40.3% lower perceived temporal demand and 37.6% lower effort. Beyond interpretability for deployment data, behavior graphs are capable progress predictors: across 43 datasets, they improve the rank correlation between predicted progress and true temporal order by 22.9% and reduce mean absolute error by 53.5% relative to the strongest baseline. As the number of deployed robots grows, behavior graphs lend structure to high-dimensional policy rollouts and make deployment data easier to interpret and reason about.

papers.title: Pure annihilation decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ with improved perturbative QCD formalism
papers.abstract: We study the pure annihilation decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ for the first time in the standard model with $S$ and $T$ representing the states of the light scalar ($1^3\!P_0$) and tensor ($1^3\!P_2$) correspondingly. Utilizing the assignment $q\bar q$ for light scalars with two-scenarios classification, we calculate the branching ratios of $B_c^+ \to ST$ with the improved perturbative QCD (iPQCD) formalism at leading order in the strong coupling $\alpha_s$. The large branching ratios around $10^{-6}$ within uncertainties in the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa-favored channels, such as $B_c^+ \to a_0(1450) a_2(1320)$, $B_c^+ \to a_0(980, 1450)^+ f_2(1270)$, $B_c^+ \to K_0^*(700, 1430) K_2^*(1430)$, and $B_c^+ \to f_0(500, 1370, 1500) a_2(1320)^+$, are obtained in the iPQCD formalism, which would be tested at the Large Hadron Collider-beauty detector in the (near) future. The relevant tests to these theoretical predictions of large branching ratios associated with typical relative ratios could provide important opportunities for understanding the QCD dynamics of the involved modes or light scalars, as well as for exploring the reliability of the iPQCD formalism. Moreover, the direct charge-parity violating asymmetries in the decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ are naturally zero, since only tree-diagram contributions are involved.

papers.title: Generalized Frobenius Structures on Hurwitz Spaces, Their Open Extensions and Associated Principal Hierarchies
papers.abstract: We construct generalized Frobenius structures on Hurwitz spaces of arbitrary genus using extended primary differentials. Through contour integrals involving the Cauchy kernel, we derive explicit dispersionless Lax representations for the principal hierarchies of these structures and their almost-dual counterparts. We also construct solutions to the open WDVV equations for both the original and almost-dual structures, and derive explicit principal hierarchies for the resulting rank-one extensions. Finally, we show that these constructions admit Shramchenko deformations.

papers.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
papers.abstract: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.

papers.title: Comparison categories: the normal form and the regularity of comparison data
papers.abstract: Many equivalence relations of mathematics (Green's relations on a semigroup, orbit relations of group actions, ``same value of an invariant'') are defined by allowed transformations, of a morphism on its two sides or of a point of a set. We put them in one framework. A comparison datum produces a category, the comparison category, whose arrows are the allowed transformations, and two morphisms are related when they can be compared in both directions. Its normal form is a Grothendieck construction, so every such relation is mutual reachability for an action; Green's relations, orbit relations and, more generally, relations defined by an invariant are worked out in detail from it. If the way morphisms are transported is an arbitrary function, every relation occurs, so the real constraint is the regularity of the transport. For completely functorial data we show that the relations obtained contain Green's relations and congruences, we study them at two opposite extremes: on finite groups (every morphism invertible) they are described through double cosets, and on nil monoids (only the unit invertible) we prove a collapse theorem. A short plain-language guide to the vocabulary (comparison categories and transport, Grothendieck construction and mutual reachability, functors, pseudofunctors and lax functors, enriched categories, colimits and stabilization) is included for readers who are not specialists.

papers.title: Prompt Lottery in LLM-as-a-Judge: Measuring and Mitigating Sensitivity to Syntactic Rephrasing
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-Judge has become a standard for evaluating large language models, yet most approaches implicitly assume that a single judge prompt functions as a stable evaluation instrument. Prior work has primarily explored deliberate prompt modifications such as scoring rubrics, role descriptions, or chain-of-thought reasoning in order to optimize accuracy. In contrast, we investigate whether validated prompt variants intended to preserve evaluation semantics while differing in surface realization (\textit{paraphrastic rephrasings}) yield consistent judgments under a fixed evaluation task. We introduce \textit{Prompt Lottery}, a phenomenon in which paraphrastic rephrasings produce different LLMaJ judgments. Across a large-scale study spanning diverse evaluation tasks, judge families, and model backbones, we find that these variations can alter evaluation outcomes and, in some settings, reverse relative model rankings. A user study with 10 human annotators shows that LLMaJ judges exhibit 6-9$\times$ larger agreement degradation under prompt rephrasings than humans, falling below the generally accepted threshold in usability studies. This indicates that single-prompt evaluation is insufficiently robust for model ranking. Finally, we show that multi-prompt aggregation substantially improves robustness by emphasizing judgments that remain consistent across prompt variants.

papers.title: Black Hole Entropy from Entangled Quantum Reference Frames
Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
Dynamical plausibility of triple-assisted interaction in Be-star multiple systems
papers.abstract: Classical Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars surrounded by gaseous circumstellar disks, but the origin of their angular momentum remains uncertain. We investigate whether observed Be-star multiple systems are dynamically compatible with triple-assisted interaction, in which a tertiary companion drives Kozai-Lidov (KL) eccentricity excitation in an unresolved inner binary. We combine speckle-interferometric detections, reported inner periods, and proper-motion anomalies (PMa) with synthetic populations of hierarchical triples. Accepted configurations must satisfy dynamical stability, secular-timescale, inner-periastron interaction, and observational constraints. Refined mass-aware simulations identify HD 35079 and HD 55606 as the clearest period-plus-speckle dynamical matches. HD 205329 remains dynamically plausible but depends on the approximate PMa constraint. For HD 41335, the period-plus-speckle and PMa-plus-speckle constraints are separately compatible, whereas imposing all three simultaneously yields no accepted configurations at the adopted tolerance. HD 37330, HD 41600, and HD 71510 are additional PMa-dependent hierarchical-triple candidates. An independent angular-momentum estimate indicates a median required accreted mass fraction of approximately 4.8% under the adopted assumptions. We conclude that several observed Be-star multiple systems admit stable, KL-active architectures capable of driving inner binaries toward interaction. These results establish dynamical plausibility rather than a confirmed evolutionary history and motivate further speckle, spectroscopic, and astrometric monitoring.

papers.title: Motivic $C_p$-power operations in $\mathrm{MGL}$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of the Hopkins-Morel-Hoyois theorem for fields $k$ of characteristic unequal to $p$ containing all primitive $p$-power roots of unity for a fixed prime $p$. This new proof follows Quillen's proof for the structure of the homotopy groups of $\mathrm{MU}$ which utilizes topological power operations. To this end we define a motivic analog of the Steenrod power operations, using the theory of normed motivic spectra as developed by Bachmann--Hoyois and their application for the definition of motivic colimits as developed by Bachmann-Elmanto-Heller.

papers.title: Energy stability of explicit--implicit--null time discretizations for a class of nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients
papers.abstract: We study a class of nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients admitting a scalar energy potential. The explicit--implicit--null (EIN) method avoids severe time step restrictions of explicit time stepping and costly Newton--Raphson iterations required by a fully implicit treatment of the nonlinearity. Using orthogonal projection of the Kirchhoff transform, we prove nonlinear energy stability for first- to third-order EIN time stepping coupled with a wide range of spatial discretizations that admit self-adjoint positive semidefinite discrete operators. Under an upper bound for the diffusion coefficient on relevant stage segments, two IMEX coefficient conditions yield sufficient stabilization bounds without any time step restriction. The estimates dissipate the original convex energy and allow degenerate diffusion. We also extend the analysis to diffusion systems with a scalar energy potential in a fixed positive definite metric, and to consistent positive-weight quadrature discretizations. Applications include porous-medium flow, nonlinear heat transfer in plasma, and multicomponent diffusion.

papers.title: A Multi-Domain Study on the Effectiveness of LLMs at Writing Property-Based Tests
papers.abstract: A property-based test (PBT) checks a property of a program on many generated inputs, but writing one takes a property, a generator of valid inputs, and an oracle. LLM-based PBT writers produce all three, yet they have been evaluated only on Python libraries. We study how two of them, Proptest-AI and Agentic-PBT, generalize to ten programs in five domains: deep learning libraries, databases, system software, compilers, and LLM serving engines. Most of these programs take text in their own language, such as queries, configurations, and programs. Agentic-PBT covers more branches than Proptest-AI on seven of the ten programs with Opus 5 and on all ten with GLM-5.3-Flash. Domain-specific fuzzers cover more of the compilers and of PostgreSQL and less of PyTorch than Agentic-PBT. We filed 180 bug reports, 44 of which duplicate reports that others filed after the models' knowledge cutoffs; maintainers have confirmed 65 of the others, in all five domains, and fixed 23. We draw lessons for building and evaluating such writers: low observability hurts them, and mature fuzzers paired with LLM-written properties could check that each feature behaves as documented.

papers.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
What Makes a Question Curious? Measuring Model Curiosity in Human-LLM Interactions
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly act as partners in everyday communication. In these interactions, useful assistance may require not only answering, but also asking the right questions that surface knowledge gaps, assumptions, and alternatives. In this study, we refer to such epistemic question-asking as model curiosity, and introduce a theory-grounded taxonomy that distinguishes curiosity-oriented questions from generic model questioning. Across four conversation datasets, we find that curiosity-oriented questions remain rare (17-28% of all questions), but are associated with more exploratory and epistemically rich subsequent user responses, with varying patterns across datasets. We further conduct a human study to evaluate the usefulness of model curiosity, finding that curiosity can encourage exploration, especially in advice, creative, and research contexts. These findings have implications for building LLMs that ask more selectively to support deeper exploration and human-AI collaboration.

papers.title: Late Epoch Infrared Spectroscopy and Two-Component 3D Photoionization Modeling of Classical Nova V5668 Sgr
papers.abstract: V5668 Sgr is an Fe II classical nova (CN) that exploded on 15 March 2015. We present near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy of the ejecta from the Mt. Abu observatory which exhibits emission lines of species H, He, N, S, Ti, and Si. We also present SOFIA (+FORCAST) spectroscopy which shows two forbidden emission lines, [Ne II] at 12.8 $\mu$m and [O IV] at 25.9 $\mu$m, as well as two emission features attributed to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) at 6.2 $\mu$m and 11.3 $\mu$m. 1D Cloudy photoionization simulations require two components to model the system, which suggests a multifaceted, morphologically complex ejecta. The 1D simulations also reveal He, N, Ne, S, Ti, Si, and O chemical abundances elevated above fiducial solar levels. 3D pyCloudy photoionization emission profiles visualize the ejecta and elucidate the system's complex composition.

papers.title: The As-If Machine: Personalized AI counterfactuals make distant policy risks feel close
papers.abstract: Life experiences can shape policy attitudes, but we only live one life. Citizens may therefore fail to support policies addressing risks they have never personally experienced. Narratives can make such risks immediate and personal, but personalized stories remain difficult to produce at scale. Here we ask whether AI can make distant scenarios feel concrete by simulating a participant's life as if that scenario occurred. We present the As-If Machine (AIM), a multi-agent system through which people co-write personalized counterfactual narratives---stories about their own lives under different policy futures. In two pre-registered and quota-matched experiments on science funding (N=1,007) and satellite cybersecurity (N=894), we compared AIM with two controls: reading an expert-written vignette on the same topic and co-writing with AIM about an unrelated topic. AIM increased psychological closeness---how close a risk feels to the self---by nearly identical margins in the two domains (0.36 and 0.38 standard deviations (SDs) against the vignette, 0.80 and 0.90 against unrelated writing). AIM increased psychological closeness even among participants with unfavorable views of AI. For policy attitudes, AIM's effects were 0.16 SDs against the vignette and 0.10 SDs (n.s.) against unrelated writing for science funding; the corresponding effects for satellite cybersecurity were 0.54 and 0.67 SDs. Across 23,496 human-AI autocomplete interactions, participants and the system played distinct roles: AIM supplied concrete detail that grounded the scenario, and participants supplied first-person perspective and emotion. Co-writing with the As-If Machine makes distant policy risks feel close.

papers.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
papers.abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

papers.title: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
Anisotropic spin hydrodynamics in a magnetized medium: entropy-current formulation and minimal linear modes
papers.abstract: We formulate anisotropic relativistic spin hydrodynamics in a parity-even magnetized medium using an Israel--Stewart entropy-current construction. Treating the magnetic field at leading order in the gradient expansion reduces the rotational symmetry to $SO(2)$ and separates spin susceptibilities and dissipative transport into longitudinal, transverse, and mixed channels. A restricted quadratic entropy current yields transient equations for the retained dissipative stresses and spin fluxes. We analyze a minimal linear closure around an unpolarized homogeneous equilibrium. Magnetic-flux perturbations remain dynamical, and spin and magnetic fluctuations mix through the fluid variables without explicit spin-magnetization coupling. Infrared coefficient equations and ultraviolet characteristic expansions organize the magnetosonic and Alfvén-like spectra together with spectator spin-flux poles. The retained first-order boost sectors are unstable already at zero wave number, and the ultraviolet spectrum includes superlinear branches. Positive effective inertias stabilize the zero-momentum gapped modes of the boost sector. For the baseline parameters, finite relaxation times yield asymptotically linear propagation branches and finite relaxation poles, with no growing modes found on the sampled grid. The characteristic speeds depend on the magnetic angle and the spin-transport ratios. We determine their relation to the light cone.

papers.title: Rotation slows the instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
papers.abstract: Rotation weakens the radial instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in slow-rotation perturbation theory. We investigate its nonlinear effect by evolving stationary rotating drainholes supported by a phantom scalar field. We construct the backgrounds with an independent spectral solver, validate them against published symmetric solutions, and identify a misprint in a published field equation that did not affect the original authors' numerical results. Evolutions perturbed only by discretization error show that rotation slows the collapse. At intermediate spins some throats expand, with the direction of departure depending on the effective perturbation. At the fastest evolved spin, the throat's areal radius shows no growing departure through evolution time $t=150$ in code units, about 28 e-folding times of the static instability, at three resolutions. Two other rapidly rotating models also show no growth over their reliable evolution intervals. Collapsing rotating throats emit an axisymmetric quadrupolar gravitational-wave burst whose energy increases between the two spins compared. Second-order initial data excite the instability through their background truncation error. The results establish slower collapse and prolonged absence of detected radial growth for the sampled asymmetric backgrounds, over finite times from initially axisymmetric data.

papers.title: Scattering in spacetime cones for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$, with a class of `mixed' nonlinearities that admit soliton solutions. We are interested in the long-time behaviour of solutions with finite, but possibly large, mass and/or energy. By a spacetime cone, we mean an open set in $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}_{x,t}$ that is invariant under dilation $(x, t) \mapsto (\alpha x, \alpha t)$ for all $\alpha > 0$. Our main result is as follows: let $u(x, t)$ be the solution with initial condition in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Let $\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}$ be the mass and energy of $u$, and let $\eta = \eta(\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}) > 0$ be sufficiently small. Let $C_\epsilon$ be the complement of $N \geq 1$ of sufficiently thin spacetime cones $\{ (x, t) \mid |x-v_jt| \leq \epsilon t \}$, where $v_1, \dots, v_N$ are fixed velocities and $\epsilon$ is sufficiently small. If the $L^\infty$ norm of $u$ in $C_\epsilon$ is $\leq \eta$, we prove that $u$ scatters in $C_{2\epsilon} \subset C_\epsilon$.

papers.title: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
papers.abstract: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model with gauge and Higgs fields regulated on a finite bosonic lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This retains the familiar continuum treatment of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes. Standard Model anomaly cancellation permits a consistent, gauge-invariant phase for the massless chiral determinant. Yukawa interactions are incorporated with a gauge-covariant spectral cutoff acting on the interaction vertices, not on the fermion propagator. Under the stated analytic conditions, the cutoff can be removed by the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, yielding a finite, exactly gauge-invariant functional integral at fixed bosonic lattice spacing and spacetime volume, including topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At zero Yukawa coupling and on smooth weak-field backgrounds, we establish agreement between the appropriately chirality-matched overlap and continuum Weyl fermion determinants up to local counterterms. We also establish reflection positivity at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta for a modified gauge-field reconstruction; its continuum equivalence with Craig's original reconstruction is not proved. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.

papers.title: REFLEX: RNA Ensemble Generation via Flexibility-Calibrated Stochastic Bridge
papers.abstract: RNA molecules often function through multiple experimentally observed conformational states. A central challenge is to capture ensemble diversity without sacrificing structural fidelity: samples may collapse toward averaged representative structures or drift into unsupported conformational regions. We introduce REFLEX (RNA Ensemble generation calibrated by FLEXibility), a sequence-conditioned generator for RNA backbone-frame ensembles based on a heteroscedastic stochastic bridge on SE(3). During training, experimental B-factors calibrate residue-wise bridge widths, exposing each observed conformer through local perturbation neighborhoods with residue-specific scales while keeping constrained regions sharper. A learned flexibility condition guides the bridge-field network to recover target conformer-specific frames from these calibrated noisy states. At inference, REFLEX uses only the input sequence, requiring no MSA-subsampling heuristics. On a multi-conformer RNA benchmark, REFLEX achieves the best precision-recall trade-off for ensemble coverage across evaluation thresholds, while recovery-stress ablations indicate gains in target-frame recovery under stronger perturbations.

papers.title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
papers.abstract: We propose and study a multi-labeling generalization of the $k$-radio labeling problem of graphs: given a graph $G$ and integers $k$ and $m$, assign to each vertex of $G$ a set of $m$ integer labels such that distinct labels assigned to a vertex differ by at least $k+1$, and the labels of any two distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ pairwise differ by at least $k+1-d(x,y)$, with $d(x,y)$ being the distance between vertices $x$ and $y$. We prove general bounds on the minimum span of such a labeling and more refined results for the case $k=1$. For paths and cycles, we derive sharp bounds on the minimum span when $k$ is small. We finally propose a conjecture for the minimum span on the path and for an almost-tight bound on the cycle.

papers.title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework leveraging knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix up to a linear transformation. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

papers.title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
papers.abstract: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity this http URL first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Descending Everest, Part I: Oracle Complexity of Convex Optimization under $(L_0,L_1)$-Smoothness
papers.abstract: For convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth functions, the curvature may grow together with the gradient norm. Therefore, even when $\|x^0-x^*\|\le R$, the gradient and the optimality gap at the starting point may be exponentially large in $L_1R$, and the bound $\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}$, known for the accelerated method on functions with Lipschitz gradient, no longer describes the complexity of the problem. We determine the oracle complexity of this class for arbitrary deterministic first-order methods: for $L_0R^2/\varepsilon\ge1$, the optimal number of oracle calls $N$ satisfies $1+N=\widetilde\Theta(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+L_1R)$. The upper bound reads $O(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(1+L_1R)\log(2+L_1R))$: the method first passes through the large-gradient regime in $O(1+L_1R)$ iterations with an inexact line search, and then the standard accelerated method with a constant stepsize takes over. The lower bound is obtained by means of chains and the orthogonal invariance principle on functions conjugate to strongly convex functions on a polytope. If the initial optimality gap is at most $4\varepsilon$, the optimal bound becomes $1+N=\widetilde\Theta(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(L_1R)^{2/3})$.

papers.title: Optimal Strategies for Gravitational-Wave Memory Detection with Noise Marginalization in Pulsar Timing Arrays
papers.abstract: Current pulsar timing arrays could detect gravitational wave memory, which would provide a unique test of general relativity. In order to optimize our searches for gravitational wave memory in pulsar timing arrays, we integrate the optimal frequentist statistics for GW memory into the \texttt{enterprise} code suite. We additionally test a noise marginalized version of this statistic, and compare it's effectiveness to the simpler maximum posterior method. We perform these tests on simulated pulsar timing array with red and white noise content, as well as the NANOGrav $15$-year data set. We find no significant variations in our detection statistics between the noise-marginalized and the maximum-posterior methods for the simulated datasets, and only small variations in the NANOGrav $15$-year comparisons. We conclude that for realistic PTAs the noise-marginalization method could be useful for assigning a false alarm probability to Bayesian results, though the maximum posterior method is sufficient for identifying potentially detectable signals.

papers.title: RoboFQE: Rollout-Free Evaluation of Visual Robot Policies from Offline Trajectories
papers.abstract: Evaluating robot policies before deployment typically requires producing new trajectories through real-world execution, simulators, or learned world models. These rollout-based approaches impose infrastructure requirements; simulator and world-model evaluators additionally face prediction errors that can compound over the evaluation horizon. In this paper, we study off-policy evaluation as an alternative to rollout-based robot-policy evaluation methods. Specifically, we introduce RoboFQE, an evaluator that estimates the discounted expected return of a target policy from offline robot trajectories without estimating a behavior-policy density, combining fitted Q-evaluation with a pretrained vision foundation model and learned terminal success annotation to bridge the gap between standard OPE benchmarks and continuous-control visual manipulation. Controlled experiments across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show that RoboFQE produces accurate discounted-return estimates and preserves policy rankings even on long-horizon manipulation tasks where video world-model evaluators are degraded by autoregressive prediction errors. Ablation experiments show that pretrained vision encoders substantially outperform from-scratch alternatives, particularly on long-horizon tasks, and that learned terminal success annotation enables evaluation without ground-truth reward labels with only slight reduction of accuracy.

papers.title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
papers.abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.

papers.title: Heavy flavour production in the presence of a weak magnetic field
papers.abstract: We calculate an analytic expression for the cross section, up to order $(eB)^2$, for heavy quark ($Q$) production of mass $m_Q$ through the gluon ($g$) fusion process $g+g \to Q+\bar{Q}$ in the presence of a constant weak external magnetic field $B$ with strength $eB \ll m_Q^2$. This is done using the weak-field expansion of the fermion propagator, calculated with Schwinger's proper-time formalism. Owing to the hierarchy of scales ($m_Q^2 \gg eB$), we neglect the effects of the magnetic field on the quark and antiquark spinors in the external lines. Since the magnetic field breaks rotational invariance, the cross section becomes anisotropic and depends on the orientation angle $\theta$ between the magnetic field and the incoming gluons in the center of mass frame. The lowest-order magnetic correction to the vacuum cross section scales as $(eB)^2$ and has $\cos 2\theta$ and $\cos 4\theta$ dependence, reflecting the breaking of rotational symmetry by the magnetic field. The cross section is maximized when the gluons propagate along the field direction ($\theta = 0, \pi$) and minimized in the perpendicular configuration ($\theta = \pi/2$). The resulting asymmetry peaks near the production threshold and falls with increasing center of mass energy, scaling as $(eB)^2/m_Q^4$ with the quark mass. These results provide direct, calculable signatures of the initial-stage magnetic field in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, which can in principle be imprinted on heavy-flavour observables measured in the final state.

papers.title: Hurricane recovery gaps lie in reconnection, not local restart
papers.abstract: Climate-intensified hurricanes disrupt urban mobility, yet whether recovery is equitable across the rural-urban gradient is unclear. Analyzing device-based mobility for Hurricanes Helene and Milton, we find local activity restarted within approximately 4.5 days in both storms, whereas reconnection to the outside world took 5 days in coastal-urban Florida but 11 in inland-rural Appalachia. The gap lies in external reconnection, not local restart, implying planners should target rural isolation.

papers.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength ($\alpha$). The effective lifetime of the sound-wave source increases for slower PTs, decreasing for faster PT with larger $\beta/H$ and rising with smaller $\alpha$. While the simulated amplitude of normalized gravitational waves is of order $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2})$, in alignment with Minkowski-spacetime results, the resulting GW spectra differ markedly from those scenarios.

papers.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
papers.abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.

papers.title: Initialization-Dependent Solution Selection by the Euler-Maruyama Scheme for a Degenerate SDE
papers.abstract: We study the Euler-Maruyama approximation of the degenerate stochastic differential equation $dX_t = |X_t|^\alpha\,dW_t$, $0 < \alpha < 1/2$, $X_0 = 0$, for which uniqueness in law fails. The Euler scheme started exactly from zero is trapped by the absorbing solution, whereas a nonzero initialization $x_h \to 0$ can select a different weak solution. We identify the initialization-dependent limiting regimes. The critical spatial scale is $r_h = h^{1/[2(1-\alpha)]}$, and the relevant depth parameter is $\Theta_h = h\log(1+\log^+(r_h/|x_h|))$. If $\Theta_h \to 0$, the scheme converges to the non-sticky weak solution. If $\Theta_h \to \theta \in (0,\infty)$, it converges to the solution that stays at zero for the deterministic time $\theta/|\log\alpha|$ and then evolves as the non-sticky solution. If $\Theta_h \to \infty$, the scheme converges to the absorbing solution. The proof is based on an exact scale-invariant Euler chain, a logarithmic exit-time law of large numbers, a discrete Tanaka occupation estimate, and a compact-uniform restart argument. Every finite deterministic delay can be obtained by a suitable vanishing initialization, while oscillating depth parameters yield process-level nonconvergence. Thus a vanishing initialization can survive in the limit as a macroscopic deterministic delay and thereby act as a solution selector for the Euler-Maruyama approximation.

papers.title: Diffusion-Steering-Based MPC with a JEPA World Action Model
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict actions and future observations, typically from a reconstruction-based representation that carries noisy, redundant information which can complicate downstream predictions. We introduce LeWAM, a bidirectional transformer for forward, backward, inverse dynamics and policy prediction, on a decoder-free JEPA latent trained end-to-end through all four modes. We see the following benefits: 1) Alignment: linear probes read robot and object state from LeWAM's latent better than from a regular Le World Model (a forward-only JEPA world model), while the latent ignores visual distractors as well as LeWM does and far better than a reconstruction-based WAM. 2) Acting: Closed-loop evaluations of LeWAM match a regular flow-matching policy trained on the same encoder at matched size, while also providing a world model. 3) Planning: Sampling raw actions when planning with WAMs lets MPC exploit dynamics-model inaccuracies; planning in the noise space of the policy head instead improves the closed-loop performance of these WAMs.

papers.title: Spurious zero-dispersion continua in full $(2,q)$-positivity: A linear hierarchy-depth lower bound from an exactly solvable counting operator
Logarithmic upper bounds and axial front selection for spatially periodic lattice Fisher--KPP equations
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=\Delta_{\Z^d}u+F(x,u)$ on $\Z^d$ ($d\geq2$) with a spatially periodic Fisher--KPP reaction $F$ and a nonzero, finitely supported initial datum $u_0:\Z^d\to[0,1]$. We establish a logarithmic upper bound on the front position that holds uniformly in the observation direction, with a logarithmic delay coefficient governed by the outward normal to the asymptotic spreading body. When the linearized growth rate $F_s(x,0)$ is independent of the longitudinal coordinate, we prove the matching axial Bramson correction and show that the solution converges uniformly on fixed-width half-tubes to a critical pulsating front up to a bounded, slowly varying phase shift. For critical pulsating profiles $\Phi(s,x)$ satisfying $\Phi(s,x)\leq C(1+s)\ee^{-\lambda s}$ for $s\geq0$ and $x\in\Z^d$, where $\lambda>0$ is the critical spatial decay rate, we derive the precise leading-edge asymptotic expansion and prove uniqueness up to translation. As a consequence, in the axial regime we obtain sharp asymptotics for the arrival times $T_\theta(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:u(t,x)\geq\theta\}$ ($0<\theta<1$), including the asymptotic time lag between distinct level sets at a remote site and the period-to-period passage time along the axis. For general periodic linearized growth rates, we introduce a nonlinear subsolution built from a positive quotient of linear Dirichlet evolutions on a retreating domain and formulate sufficient kernel estimates for a matching directional lower bound.

papers.title: Strict non-tightness of the level-3 quantum bootstrap for a coupled three-dimensional double well, at an excited eigenstate
papers.abstract: For the coupled three-dimensional double well $H=\tfrac12|p|^2+2\sum_i(q_i^2-1)^2-\sum_{i<j}q_i^2q_j^2$ we exhibit, at the first excited energy level (and also at the ground state), a linear functional on polynomials of degree $\le 6$ that satisfies every constraint of the standard level-3 eigenstate bootstrap, has a strictly positive definite moment matrix, and nevertheless assigns a negative value to a nonnegative polynomial. It is therefore an interior point of the level-3 relaxation that is realized by no quantum state. The construction reflects a fact that holds at every level: the eigenstate rows never reach the top-degree momentum moments. At level 3, where strictly feasible points exist, this means that the corresponding block of the moment matrix carries no information about which energies admit one. Every algebraic ingredient is an exact rational certificate, and the only numerical ingredients (spectral enclosures of an eigenfunction) are carried out in rigorous ball arithmetic.

papers.title: Betti Numbers of Odd Biisotropic Symplectic Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We compute the singular cohomology groups of odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k, 2n+1)$ by presenting an explicit dimension-preserving combinatorial bijection between the Bialynicki-Birula cells in $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k, 2n+1)$ and the Schubert cells in $\operatorname{Gr}(k, 2n+2-k)$.

papers.title: Cubic arithmetic-geometric mean and isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves
papers.abstract: We construct degree-three isogenies of Hesse elliptic curves over an arbitrary field of characteristic different from three, which correspond to a step of the cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. As an application, we describe the Serre-Tate canonical lift of an ordinary elliptic curve in characteristic three by the 3-adic cubic arithmetic-geometric mean. We also discuss the relations of the Hesse curves with complex and finite hypergeometric functions.

papers.title: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
papers.abstract: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The proof in \cite{Sze} crucially relies on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the scalar wave equation and for Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. In addition, two results in \cite{Sze}, concerning the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}, are stated without proofs. The goal of the present paper companion paper to \cite{Sze} is to provide the proof of these two results.

papers.title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.

papers.title: PhyProbe: Rethinking Physical Consistency Evaluation in Generated Videos
papers.abstract: Evaluating the physical consistency of generated videos remains a fundamental challenge. Existing approaches rely on off-the-shelf vision-language models, which can often be myopic to physical dynamics, or fine-tuned evaluators trained on human annotations, which overfit to dataset-specific cues and fail to generalize. A key challenge is that existing supervision sources provide either relative ordering or absolute scores, but not both reliably and consistently across varied settings. To this end, we introduce PhyProbe, an evaluator that extracts features from a frozen pretrained spatio-temporal encoder and maps them to a scalar physical consistency violation score via a lightweight scoring head. PhyProbe is trained through a unified objective combining pairwise ranking, regression on noisy scalar annotations, and anchor-based calibration over a curated set of heterogeneous supervision sources. Experiments show that PhyProbe outperforms prior methods on most pairwise benchmarks spanning real-generated and generated-generated pairs under varying correspondence, with the largest gains in no-correspondence and generated-generated settings where existing fine-tuned evaluators degrade sharply. PhyProbe achieves strong correlation with human judgments, with close agreement between rank-based and linear metrics, indicating that scores are both well ordered and anchored to a stable [0, 1] scale. Further, despite being trained on supervision indicative of physical consistency, without explicit general-preference labels, PhyProbe also performs competitively on human preference benchmarks: consistent with the observation that physics violations are entangled with broader quality degradations.

papers.title: Aigner's majorization conjecture in quantitative group testing: counterexamples and eventual sufficiency for star forests
papers.abstract: We refute Aigner's majorization conjecture for star forests in adaptive quantitative group testing with two defective items. Each test counts the defectives in a chosen subset; the possible defective pairs form the edges of a star forest. Aigner's necessary majorization condition is sufficient through five tests but is not sufficient at any budget from six onward. Nevertheless, for every fixed number of stars, it becomes sufficient once the test budget is large enough. We prove that majorization is sufficient for all forests with at most twenty-nine stars, and that this bound is sharp. We also construct counterexamples that pass arbitrarily many successive compatibility checks based on majorization. The five-test converse, counterexamples, eventual sufficiency theorem and unbounded-delay construction have analytic proofs. The sharp finite support bounds also use exact integer-inequality certificates.

papers.title: Structure of derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings
papers.abstract: In this article, we study derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in torsion-free profinite rings regarded as discrete rings. We compare each such algebra with the degreewise inverse limit of the derived Hecke algebras with coefficients in finite rings and with its subalgebra consisting of elements with uniformly finite double-coset support. Under cohomological comparison hypotheses, the natural map to this subalgebra has image given by its degree-zero part and its positive-degree torsion. We describe the kernel in terms of continuous cohomology and prove that it is a divisible square-zero ideal annihilated by every positive-degree element. These comparisons are compatible with Yoneda products, and the action on torsion Ext classes factors through the image. We compute the resulting algebras for the additive group $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and determine the underlying graded abelian groups for $(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p),\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}_p))$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, for $p>3$. The examples exhibit distinct effects of the coefficient topology and the support condition.

papers.title: Simple Extensions of Single-Objective Acquisition Functions and Hedge Strategies for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) is commonly approached through specialized acquisition functions or scalarization schemes designed to explicitly account for trade-offs among non-preferential objectives. In this work, we show that such complexity might be unnecessary. We propose a framework that extends standard single-objective acquisition functions directly to the multi-objective setting through a hypervolume-based methodology. We further extend hedge strategies for acquisition functions, which are typically used only in single-objective optimization, to the multi-objective regime. Our approach requires minimal modification to existing Bayesian optimization pipelines and avoids the need for bespoke multi-objective formulations. We demonstrate how a broad class of commonly used single-objective acquisition functions and hedge strategies can be adapted in a principled manner to handle multiple objectives, while preserving their intuitive interpretation and computational efficiency. Empirically, we evaluate the proposed methods across a range of synthetic and real-world multi-objective benchmarks. Despite their simplicity, our extensions consistently match or outperform more complex state-of-the-art MOBO methods in terms of optimization performance and sample efficiency. These results suggest that effective multi-objective Bayesian optimization can be achieved by reusing and carefully extending well-established single-objective acquisition strategies, offering a simpler and more flexible alternative to existing approaches.

papers.title: Quantum error mitigation from information dynamics
papers.abstract: Overcoming experimental errors is a central challenge in quantum science. This challenge is particularly acute in large and complex quantum circuits, where quantum information spreads into exponentially many paths, foiling any direct attempt to understand errors' impact. In this work, we present a novel approach to understanding and mitigating experimental errors, based on a surprisingly compact representation of a quantum circuit's information dynamics, the reactivity function. The shape of a circuit's reactivity function governs its noise response, and its amenability to different error mitigation methods. From this viewpoint, we introduce two complementary such methods. The first, Pauli-path zero-noise extrapolation, fits a parameterized model to a circuit's reactivity function and uses it to accurately extrapolate to zero noise. The second, tunable error cancellation, filters a circuit's reactivity function to cancel noise on all information up to a threshold locality. Crucially, both methods feature a tuning parameter that allows one to systematically improve their accuracy until convergence. Across three circuit families from published experiments, our methods overcome conventional zero-noise extrapolation biases as large as 30%; at $\sim$$10^{-2}$ root-mean-square error, they reduce sampling cost relative to probabilistic error cancellation by up to a factor of $10^3$.

papers.title: Panoptic Scene Program Diffusion Transformer
papers.abstract: Modern text-to-image models produce high-fidelity images but still struggle with compositional prompts that require instance identity, attribute ownership, counting, spatial ordering, and role-sensitive relations. We introduce Panoptic Scene Program Diffusion Transformer (PSP-DiT), a diffusion-transformer architecture that treats a panoptic scene program as a first-class latent variable rather than an external control signal or post-hoc parse. PSP-DiT jointly denoises image latents and scene-program latents through coupled transformer streams, while panoptic grounding and cycle-consistency objectives tie object instances, attributes, relations, and counts to visual support in the generated image. Under matched training and inference settings, PSP-DiT improves over a strong flat-text baseline across GenEval 2, SANEval-Simple, PSG-Score, and DetailMaster, with the largest gains on counting, attribute binding, role-sensitive relations, and long structured prompts. The method preserves image quality, adds modest inference overhead, and remains robust to imperfect scene programs.

papers.title: Constraining the Quadratic-mode Amplitude Coupling in GW250114
papers.abstract: Detecting quadratic quasi-normal modes in black hole ringdowns would provide evidence for nonlinear gravitational dynamics, while measuring their properties would enable tests of the corresponding predictions of general relativity. Specifically, second-order black hole perturbation theory predicts that their amplitudes scale with the product of the amplitudes of their parent linear modes, with a coupling coefficient that depends on the spin of the remnant black hole. This mode-specific coupling coefficient has not yet been directly measured from gravitational wave data. Here, we use Bayesian inference on the GW250114 ringdown, modeled with the $220$, $221$, and $220\times220$ modes, to infer the amplitude-coupling coefficient of the $220\times220$ mode. The inferred coefficient is consistent with predictions from numerical relativity fits and second-order perturbation theory; no comparison shows a deviation exceeding $1.3 \sigma$. Although the current data cannot distinguish among these spin-dependent predictions, this measurement establishes a basis for more stringent observational tests of nonlinear gravitational dynamics in black-hole ringdowns.

papers.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
papers.abstract: We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$. Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.

papers.title: Geometric Detection and Finiteness of Log Crystalline Local Systems
papers.abstract: We prove a geometric detection theorem for log crystalline local systems in the smooth proper setting with a normal crossings boundary. The associated special-fiber log $F$-isocrystal detects geometric absolute irreducibility and, modulo constant rank-one twists, determines the pullback to the geometric generic fiber. The main ingredient is a determinant argument combining a finite-order rank-one reduction, logarithmic period comparison, and the Plücker embedding. As an application, using Abe--Esnault's finiteness theorem and finiteness of stable lattices, we prove finiteness, up to geometrically constant rank-one twists, of geometrically absolutely irreducible log crystalline local systems of fixed rank. Coefficients may lie in any fixed finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, and no bound on the Hodge--Tate weights is imposed.

papers.title: Local conservation laws, symmetries and Hamiltonian structure of three-dimensional incompressible Euler flow
papers.abstract: All smooth local conservation laws, symmetries and adjoint symmetries of three-dimensional homogeneous incompressible Euler flow are classified in the primitive velocity--pressure variables. Explicit dependence on time and position and arbitrary finite orders of mixed time and spatial derivatives are allowed. Up to trivial currents, the conservation laws consist of incompressibility, linear and angular momentum, kinetic energy, helicity and generalised time-dependent momentum. Every local adjoint symmetry is represented by a multiplier of these currents. Every finite-order local symmetry is equivalent on solutions to a classical point symmetry, resolving a conjecture of Olver. An explicit local first-order Hamiltonian structure of the primitive system is also established in the geometric theory of partial differential equations. It maps the energy multiplier to time translation; its kernel on local adjoint symmetries is spanned by the helicity and incompressibility multipliers. The proof first excludes higher-order symmetries by comparing their responses to transverse and harmonic characteristic directions in compatible derivative data. The Hamiltonian map and its kernel then determine all local adjoint symmetries from the symmetry classification. Exact multiplier identities and the correspondence between multipliers and current classes complete the conservation-law classification.

papers.title: The Science Potential of Characterizing Gas Giant Exoplanets with HWO
authors: Shelley Wright (1) ((1) University of California San Diego
papers.abstract: With the ability to directly image Earth-like exoplanets and search their atmospheres for biosignatures, the upcoming Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) will also collect high signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) reflected-light photometry and spectra of nearby gas giant exoplanets. Such high-quality data would allow investigations into the formation and evolution of low-mass, low-temperature gas giants, and could enable the detection of exomoons around these planets. We use the EXOSIMS direct imaging mission simulator to model HWO observations of Jupiter-radius gas giants at Earth-like and Jupiter-like instellations around the 164 stars in the ExEP target list. We find that HWO should be able to achieve S/N $\geq$ 5 broadband visible-light detections of gas giants in this instellation range within 5 minutes of integration. 10 hours of R=1000 near-IR spectroscopy with HWO should reveal water, methane, and ammonia absorption features in the atmospheres of Jupiter-like gas giants. HWO time-series photometry should exceed 1% flux precision in one hour for any Earth-instellation gas giants around ExEP stars, and for Jupiter-like gas giants at $d\leq$ 7 parsecs. Time-series light curves at this cadence and precision could, over tens of hours, reveal rotation-induced variability comparable to Jupiter's.
